The Reference ignores the cystatin C value completely. For the typical man it is 52.34 for any value from 0.6 to 63.75 (`units.out.txt`).

## 2. Dashboard rolling average

- **It averages values first, then computes once.** `averageBiomarkers` (`rolling-average-ba.ts:159-183`) takes a plain mean per `biomarker_key` over every row of every lab in the window. The window is 6 months with at least 2 labs, else 12 months, else the latest lab alone (`:224-247`). It then computes the Comprehensive, falling back to the Reference (`:269-296`).
- **It ignores units.** Only `biomarker_key` and `value` are fetched (`:147-157`).
- **Supplements come from the latest context version** (`:185-198`), whenever each lab was drawn.
- **One lab with cystatin C removes creatinine from every lab in the window.** The averaged panel contains cystatin C, so the drop rule deletes creatinine averaged across all labs and skips the creatine offset (`rolling.out.txt`):
  - Two EVA labs give 47.30 (man) / 46.45 (woman). Adding an upload that contains only cystatin C gives 47.90 / 47.10.
  - With creatine 5 g/day: 46.59 → 47.90 (man, +1.31) and 45.32 → 47.10 (woman, +1.78).
  - This lasts until that lab leaves the window. Because `current_ba` is cached, the change only appears at the user's next processing event.
- **eGFR from a single upload is combined with creatinine averaged across all labs.** Adding an upload with creatinine 1.10 alone moves the man's figure 47.30 → 47.40. Adding eGFR 85 (consistent with that creatinine) moves it to 51.40: **+4.0 years from eGFR** (woman +2.25; `r3.out.txt`).
- **Legacy eGFR keys are averaged separately.** `egfr` and `egfr_creatinine_based` average as two keys, then the adapter keeps one and silently drops the other (`rolling.out.txt` R7). I could not check whether any legacy `egfr` rows exist.

## 3. Explain module and what clients are told

- **`biological-age-explain.ts` is internal only.** Its header says "Nothing here is stored or shown to users" (`:1-3`). Its only users are tests, `scripts/kdm_explain_panels.ts` and `docs/biomarker-evidence/longevity/KDM-EXPLAIN-PANELS.md`; no UI or API route imports it.
- **It matches the real behaviour by construction**, because it reuses `applyLifestyleAdjustments` and `resolveKdmParams` (`:170-172`):
  - S2 Reference: no filtration marker in the contributions.
  - S2 Comprehensive: cystatin C +0.40 years.
  - It never states that creatinine was removed.
  - Its comment "creatinine replaced by Cystatin C" (`:98-100`) is wrong for the Reference, where nothing replaces it.
  - In `KDM-EXPLAIN-PANELS.md:30`, eGFR is the largest single contributor (+9.5 years, athlete).
- **Pages clients actually read:**
  - **Methodology page** (`metodologia/page.tsx:80` ES, `:151` EN). Accurate for the Reference. "In place of creatinine" for the Comprehensive is incomplete: when the lab reports eGFR, creatinine's information comes back through eGFR (S5).
  - **Full methodology page** (`metodologia/completa/page.tsx:127/243`): "8 of 14 … with albumin and creatinine (or cystatin C) mandatory". This describes the gate, but hides that the Reference can then run on 7 markers (S8). The same page (`:95/211`) says mortality testing required albumin and creatinine, which is true of the validation.
  - **Lab page:** shows the stored Reference figure (`labs/page.tsx:44`, `labs-client.tsx:927-933`) with no note about creatinine.
  - **Results email:** only the upload route sends the Reference figure (`confirm/route.ts:240-257`, template `results-ready.ts:22/40`). That is exactly the path by which cystatin C arrives. The Echevarne paths send `biologicalAge: null` (`[id]/context/route.ts:187-198`, `auto-resolve.ts:132`).
  - **AI chat:** reads the stored Reference figure (`api/ai/chat/route.ts:40`).
  - **Dashboard:** shows `current_ba` with `n_markers_used` (`dashboard-client.tsx:300-306, 409-428, 1167-1173`).

## 4. History

- **When the rule came in:** commit **1cb3c2b** (PR #32, 26 May 2026), in the squashed sub-commit "creatine-aware creatinine offset + Cystatin-C-preferred kidney". `git log -S 'Cystatin-C-preferred'` shows only this commit and 64acdac. 64acdac is a parentless root commit that re-imports the repo (501 files) on 25 August 2026; it is not a second introduction.
- **Why it was added:** the stated reason is "Cystatin C is the strictly better kidney aging biomarker … unaffected by muscle mass or creatine supplementation". It arrived alongside the creatine offset, prompted by a production user taking creatine 10 g/day.
  - No validation run is mentioned; the new tests cover `supplements.ts` only.
  - The gate's comment "(Path B / v2.2.1 addition)" (`biological-age-kdm.ts:613`) has nothing to do with the Path B refit.
  - EVA's own sources contradict "unaffected": cystatin C varies with smoking, body size, inflammation and thyroid function (`supabase/seed-data/biomarker-sources.json:13253`).
  - The May 2026 methodology page (c0e6931) said "unaffected by muscle mass"; 118d51a (29 October 2026) added the Reference caveat (counsel note `METHODOLOGY-CLAIMS-FOR-COUNSEL.md:63-65`).
- **The rule is absent from every Python pipeline:**
  - `comprehensive_ba_mortality_validation.py`: MANDATORY = Albúmina + Creatinina (`:47`); the gate and estimator (`:144-176`) have no cystatin C logic; the Comprehensive uses every library marker present in the table (`:249`).
  - `honest_holdout_validation.py:38, 94-132`; it hard-codes 1.391 and 1.654 at `:283-284`.
  - `path_b_mortality_revalidation.py:48`, `hybrid_path_b_validation.py:31`, `kdm_panel_revalidation.py:67, 147-150` (runbook `kdm-panel-revalidation.md:29-30`).
  - The parity fixture builder (`build_kdm_parity_fixture.py:50-89`) has no gate and no drop.
  - Fixture `kdm-python-parity.json`: case "all" (`:127`) contains Creatinina (`:131`), TFGe (`:188`) and Cistatina C (`:190`), and expects 81 markers (`:215`), i.e. all three used together.
- **HR 1.39 and 1.65 were computed without the rule.** They come from configuration C of `comprehensive_ba_mortality_validation.py` (commit bb148a2). Creatinine was required for everyone. The Reference never saw cystatin C. The Comprehensive used creatinine + eGFR for everyone, plus cystatin C where measured. No creatine offset was applied.
- **Two further differences from the deployed model:**
  - Creatinine kept its library parameters in that run (`:94-107`). Its deployed weight is 0.48× (men) and 0.42× (women) of the validated weight.
  - For pooled markers such as cystatin C, the run used its on-the-fly NHANES refit, which returns its own q (`:118-122`), not the Spanish q the app uses.
- **Did the validation data contain cystatin C?** Probably yes, for at most 1,664 subjects (about 9% or less of 18,570). The Path B generator reads the same parquet file (`generate_path_b_full_overrides.py:22, 56, 59`) and found n=1,664 cystatin C values (`path_b_overrides.json:768`). The file itself is on the developer's machine, so I could not confirm this.
- **eGFR in the training data:** its n is 18,632, identical to creatinine's 9,186 + 9,446, and the library note says "CKD-EPI calculated" (`marker_library_v2_2.json:4007, 4011`). This fits eGFR having been computed from creatinine for every subject; the equation used is not recorded.
- **Wrong cycle label:** the library lists cystatin C cycles as "1999-2002, 2007-2018" (`:4195`). EVA's own NHANES inventory has none after 2004 (`ml/biological-age/addons/DATA-INVENTORY.md:60-75`), so the label is probably wrong (not verified).
- **The only outcome-data run that applied the rule:** the version 3 baseline harness ran the production Reference with cystatin C (`REPORT-baselines.md:253`). Its T5 check records "creatinine (male, all_available): 0.00 y" (`harness/results/baselines.md:129`).

| Test | What it asserts | Under a fix |

Holds if cystatin C replaces creatinine in both versions (`explain_cf.out.txt`) |
| `biological-age-explain.test.ts:92` | case "woman 52, Cystatin C replaces creatinine" (`:98-107`) | Assertions are self-consistent and survive any fix applied through the shared functions; the label becomes wrong |
| `biological-age-kdm.test.ts:841-923` | eGFR 95 and cystatin C 0.9 at `:870-871`; checks at `:909-922` | Hold under all four alternative rules. Today: Reference 48.92 with no filtration marker, Comprehensive 47.60 (`tests_cf.out.txt`) |
| `kdm-adapter.test.ts:213-221` (and `:223-227`) | `cystatin_c` listed as not a seed key, i.e. no canonical unit | Changes if cystatin C gets a seed unit, which a unit gate needs |
| `biological-age-kdm.test.ts:666-713` | gate tests, none with cystatin C | Nothing tests the substitution, the +1 count or the drop itself, so removing them breaks no test |
| Parity test `biological-age-kdm.parity.test.ts:53-94` | calls `klemeraDoubalBa` directly with library parameters | Unaffected unless the library JSON changes |
| `spanish-recalibration.test.ts:140-201` | panels include eGFR | An eGFR change could move these; not run |
| `process-results.*.test.ts` | expectations come from the same functions | Follow any fix |
| Generated docs | `KDM-EXPLAIN-PANELS.md` panels include eGFR; the version 3 baseline KDM "all_available" rows (`baselines.md:21,35,49,63`) | Would change under an eGFR or cystatin C fix |

## 6. Version 3

- **Version 3 always uses creatinine and ignores cystatin C.** The tiers are albumin, ALP, hs-CRP, creatinine, BUN and GGT (± HbA1c) (`biological-age-v3.ts:43-44`, `ba_v3_model.json`); other keys are ignored (`:55-56`, `:382`). It applies no creatine offset (no supplement code in the v3 files).
- **Its documents:** cystatin C "not tested, too little NHANES data" (`PROPOSAL.md:126`); "exploratory and was not used" (`MODEL-CARD.md:106`); a future UK Biobank add-on (`PROPOSAL.md:173`). Under v3, tests from other laboratories do not enter the age (`PROPOSAL.md:45`), and cystatin C only ever comes from other laboratories.
- **The shadow write does not depend on KDM inputs.** It receives the stored rows (`process-results.ts:609`, `values: biomarkerValuesToInsert`) or reads `biomarker_values` itself (`:771`; `biological-age-v3-adapter.ts:619-627`). It runs after the KDM write and cannot change it.

## 7. Where results are stored

- **Per lab** (`lab_results`):
  - Written in `processLabResults` (`process-results.ts:584-591`) and `recomputeLabMetrics` (`:739-753`).
  - Fields: `biological_age` (Reference), `bio_age_method` (always "KDM_v2.2_ReferenceBA"), `bio_age_n_markers`, `bio_age_applied_spanish_calibration`, `biological_age_comprehensive`.
  - The Reference is also copied into the result object used by the email and API responses (`:556-575`).
- **Per client:** `profiles.current_ba*`, written by `recomputeAndCacheUserBA` (`rolling-average-ba.ts:308-326`) and called at `process-results.ts:616` and `:775`.
- **What triggers a recompute:** uploads (confirm), the webhook, the lab bridge, admin entry, reprocessing, value edits and regenerate-summary (through `regenerate-master.ts:102`), and the admin recalc route (`recalc-metrics/route.ts:56`, not run). Offline: `scripts/compute_kdm_backfill.ts` (compute only) and `scripts/backfill_rolling_average_ba.ts`.
- **What a code change does without a recalculation:**
  - Old lab rows and emails already sent keep the old values.
  - Each client's dashboard figure is recomputed from all labs in the window **at that client's next processing event**: an implicit partial recalculation.
  - No column records which rule produced a value; only `current_ba_computed_at` (`rolling-average-ba.ts:320`) can be compared with deploy dates.
- **Nothing client-facing recomputes on the fly.** Pages read stored or cached values; only internal scripts call `explainBiologicalAge`.
- **Sizing the affected group:** for example `count(distinct lab_result_id) where biomarker_key='cystatin_c'`. **Not run** (database access is out of scope).

## 8. Other defects in this area

1. **The gate counts a marker the Reference does not use.** S8 and S3b give a Reference on 7 of 14 markers.
   - The docs still say creatinine is mandatory (`biological-age-kdm.ts:109-113, 141, 843-844`; `process-results.ts:539-545`; `rolling-average-ba.ts:30`).
   - `MANDATORY_BASE_MARKERS` (`:593-596`) is never used.
2. **eGFR is counted twice and dominates the Comprehensive.**
   - eGFR is a function of creatinine, so creatinine's information enters twice when a report includes eGFR.
   - eGFR has 15.8–25.7 times creatinine's weight. One reported eGFR moves the dashboard figure by 2–4 years.
   - eGFR is not dropped when cystatin C is present, which defeats the drop rule's purpose (S5).
   - The creatine offset never reaches eGFR. Recomputing eGFR from the offset creatinine would move the Comprehensive by −5.3 years (man) and −4.8 (woman) (`egfr_creatine.out.txt`, using CKD-EPI 2021 as quoted in `biomarker-sources.json:13239`).
   - At fixed creatinine, CKD-EPI 2021 falls 0.59–0.62 mL/min per year, about 70–74% of k. My inference: most of eGFR's slope with age is the equation's own age term, which feeds age back into the estimate.
   - EVA's own laboratory reports no eGFR (not in the Echevarne catalog or mapping), so the Comprehensive changes estimator depending on whether a client's report printed eGFR.
3. **An uploaded cystatin C gets no unit or plausibility check.**
   - No spelling of cystatin C is recognised automatically (`name-matcher.ts:20-66`; `units.out.txt`). It enters only when the client picks it manually, which clears the implausibility flag (`upload-client.tsx:800-804`).
   - The key has no canonical unit (`getCanonicalUnit` returns null; not in the seed), so the unit gate at `process-results.ts:355-375` is skipped, and `convertBiomarker` passes nmol/L or mg/dL through unchanged.
   - 63.75 (that is, nmol/L) gives a Comprehensive of **269 years**.
   - The `plausibility_bounds.json:72` bounds for cystatin C (0.2–8.0 mg/L) are read by no code.
   - The `cystatin_c` reference row exists only in production; both migrations only UPDATE it (`20260923000000:40,68`; `20260925000000:45,63`).
   - NHANES' 1999–2002 cystatin C assay predates current standardisation, and the CDC warns its calibration varied (`DATA-INVENTORY.md:81`). Size of the effect not verified.
4. **The cystatin C intercept mixes two sources.** The Spanish q (0.428 = 0.809 × the library q) is combined with Path B's k and s. The model then expects 0.736 mg/L at age 45, below EVA's optimal ceiling of 0.85, so a value at that ceiling reads about 0.7 years older in the Comprehensive. Path B's own q would give 0.910 instead.
5. **The creatine offset uses the latest supplements, not the lab's own context snapshot** (`process-results.ts:523-537`, `rolling-average-ba.ts:185-198`). Reprocessing an old lab therefore applies today's creatine status.

## Appendix: the same estimator under four alternative kidney rules

From `tests_cf.out.txt`. Each cell is Reference / Comprehensive, for: cystatin C added | cystatin C added with creatine 5 g/day.

| Rule | Man 45 | Woman 45 |
|---|---|---|
| Current | 52.34 / 47.90 \| 52.34 / 47.90 | 48.85 / 47.10 \| 48.85 / 47.10 |
| Keep creatinine; cystatin C in Comprehensive only (matches validation) | 51.29 / 47.54 \| 49.59 / 46.84 | 47.83 / 46.63 \| 45.63 / 45.53 |
| Ignore cystatin C | 51.29 / 47.20 \| 49.59 / 46.49 | 47.83 / 46.29 \| 45.63 / 45.16 |
| Reference keeps creatinine; Comprehensive swaps to cystatin C | 51.29 / 47.90 \| 49.59 / 47.90 | 47.83 / 47.10 \| 45.63 / 47.10 |
| Swap to cystatin C in both versions | 52.87 / 47.90 \| 52.87 / 47.90 | 49.44 / 47.10 \| 49.44 / 47.10 |

Only "current" and "swap to cystatin C in both versions" give a result for S3 or S3b (no creatinine). The other three return none for those cases, as the validation gate would.

# Current numbers: KDM v2.2.2 with cystatin C, measured on the deployed code (label: current-numbers)

Run on 29 October 2026 against the deployed code with no changes. The repo is untouched (`git status` is clean). No database, no API routes, synthetic panels only.

**Scripts and outputs.** All are in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-eva-health/4e1a7523-c199-547a-904f-d87e53286958/scratchpad/cysc/current-numbers/`. Run each from the repo root with `cd /home/user/eva-health && npx tsx <path>`.
- `common.ts`: shared helpers and the CKD-EPI 2021 and 2012 equations.
- `grid.ts`: writes `grid.md` (every one of the 336 cases with Reference and Comprehensive BA, BA_E, s_BA, number of markers, kidney markers used and gate count), `grid.csv` (full precision) and `grid-condensed.md`. Its built-in checks all pass.
- `compact.ts`: writes `compact.md`, the R and C tables below. It asserts which grid dimensions never change the result.
- `weights.ts`: writes `weights.md`, item (a).
- `typical.ts`: writes `typical.md`, item (c).
- `match.ts`: tests how the upload name-matcher maps cystatin C and eGFR names.

**Setup**
- **Panels.** "Base" is the panel's values for the 13 Base Panel keys plus fructosamine 200 µmol/L, as `scripts/base_panel_assessment.ts` does. The model sets that fructosamine aside; I checked it changes nothing (largest BA difference 0). "Full" is every panel value plus fructosamine 200.
- **eGFR.** I removed each panel's own eGFR. "Present" means CKD-EPI 2021 race-free, computed from the panel's measured creatinine, sex and age, then rounded: 95, 100, 87, 78, 69, 91 and 104. The paper is Inker et al., NEJM 2021;385:1737-49, PMID 34554658, DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa2102953. The coefficients are 142 × min(Scr/κ,1)^α × max(Scr/κ,1)^−1.200 × 0.9938^age × 1.012 if female; κ 0.7 (women) / 0.9 (men); α −0.241 (women) / −0.302 (men).
- **Creatine.** The code expects `supplements: [{key:"creatine", dose:"5g"}]` (supplements.ts:38-41, 177-190), which gives an offset of 0.175 mg/dL.
- **Checks.** The scripts reproduce NUMBERS.md section C (man 51.3 / 47.2 / 45.0 / 46.4; woman 47.8 / 46.3 / 44.8 / 41.8). They also reproduce the task's figures: man 52.3 Reference and 47.9 Comprehensive, woman 48.9 and 47.1, with cystatin C 0.85.

## Findings
1. **The Reference ignores the cystatin C value.** It is identical for every value from 0.70 to 1.50 mg/L, with or without eGFR, and with or without creatine once cystatin C is present (asserted in `compact.ts`). So the defect is simply the effect of deleting creatinine. Without creatine it adds between −1.68 and +1.54 years on the Base Panel and between −1.49 and +0.89 on the full panel (table b).
2. **The defect is bigger for creatine users.** The creatine offset is skipped too: biological-age-kdm.ts:778-784 returns before the offset at :786-792. With 5 g/day declared, the defect is +2.75 to +3.76 years on the Base Panel and +1.86 to +2.52 on the full panel. The athlete is the exception at +0.02 and −0.16.
3. **Whether the Reference goes up or down depends on how the person's creatinine reads.** With the code's parameters (Spanish q plus Path B k), a typical creatinine reads young: the man's 1.0 mg/dL reads as age 25.6 and the woman's 0.75 as 28.4. Deleting it therefore raises the Reference for 6 of the 7 personas. The athlete's 1.25 reads as 87.8, so deleting it lowers his.
4. **The gate counts a marker the Reference doesn't use.** `countBasePanelMarkers` counts cystatin C in creatinine's slot (biological-age-kdm.ts:653-656), so the gate count stays the same while the Reference uses one marker fewer.
   - The vitamin D woman of 38 on the Base Panel passes the gate at 8 with only 7 markers used.
   - The metabolic syndrome and vitamin D personas have no BUN, so with cystatin C they get a Reference that uses no kidney marker at all.
5. **The Comprehensive does use cystatin C, and higher values raise the BA.** Under the code's parameters a typical cystatin C at age 45 is only 0.736 mg/L. A value of 0.85, which is the upper limit of EVA's optimal range (migration 20260925000000:63) and inside Echevarne's 0.62–1.11 reference range, reads as age 61.6 at any age.
   - At 0.85 the Comprehensive goes up by 0.31 to 0.87 years for 5 personas. It goes down by 0.04 to 0.24 for the athlete and the woman of 70, whose creatinine reads old.
   - At 1.50 every persona goes up, by 0.85 to 3.31 years.
6. **The kidney parameters are mixed from two fits.**
   - Cystatin C's q in use is 0.4284. That is the Comas slope 0.8089 applied to the library q of 0.5297, then paired with Path B's k of 0.006843, whose own q is 0.6025. As a result every cystatin C value reads 25.4 years older than on Path B's own line, and 8.6 years older than if the slope had been applied to Path B's q.
   - Creatinine goes the other way: it reads 22.5 years younger than on Path B's line for men and 16.6 for women.
   - Clinically, the typical man's creatinine of 1.0 (eGFRcr 94.6) and a cystatin C of 0.85 (eGFRcys 102 by CKD-EPI 2012) mean about the same kidney function. The model reads them as 25.6 and 61.6 years.
7. **When eGFR is present it dominates the Comprehensive, and the cystatin C rule does not remove creatinine's effect.**
   - eGFR's information weight (k/s)² is 2.747e-3, against 1.068e-4 for creatinine in men, 1.742e-4 in women, and 1.587e-4 for cystatin C. That is 26, 16 and 17 times more.
   - On the man's Base Panel, eGFR holds 65.6% of the summed weight while creatinine holds 2.5%.
   - If the lab computes eGFR from creatinine, 92–93% of creatinine's effect on the Comprehensive goes through eGFR. For the man on the Base Panel that is +4.27 years per 0.1 mg/dL in total against +0.29 directly.
   - With cystatin C present, creatinine still moves the Comprehensive by +3.97 years per 0.1 mg/dL through eGFR, so the "drop creatinine" rule removes only about 7% of its effect.
   - The athlete's Base Panel Comprehensive goes from 37.9 to 47.1 when eGFR is added, and cystatin C 0.85 barely changes that (46.9).
8. **Creatine and eGFR.** Assume creatine raises creatinine by exactly the code's own 0.175 mg/dL and the lab computes eGFR from the raised value. Then a client who declares creatine still gets a Comprehensive BA higher than the same person off creatine:

   | Panel | Man | Woman |
   |---|---|---|
   | Base Panel | +5.85 | +7.57 |
   | Full panel | +4.15 | +4.13 |

   The same happens with cystatin C present. Without eGFR the excess is 0, and the Reference is never affected.
9. **How cystatin C and eGFR reach the model.**
   - Echevarne's cystatin C test (CISTC, result I0650, mg/L, reference 0.62–1.11, catalogue line 107) is deliberately left unmapped (echevarne.ts:58).
   - The Echevarne catalogue has no eGFR result code, so EVA's own labs never send eGFR.
   - The upload name-matcher returns nothing for "Cistatina C", "Cystatin C", "CISTATINA C SUERO" and "cystatin_c" (`match.ts`). "eGFR", "CKD-EPI" and "Filtrado glomerular estimado" all match automatically to `egfr_creatinine_based` (name-matcher.ts:176-179).
   - So cystatin C can only enter when a client picks it by hand. The confirm route accepts it if `cystatin_c` exists in `biomarker_references` (confirm/route.ts:109-135).
10. **The dashboard applies the rule to a multi-lab average.** `averageBiomarkers` averages each marker across all labs in the 6- or 12-month window (rolling-average-ba.ts:165-188), then the Comprehensive is computed on that average (:270). So one cystatin C result anywhere in the window removes creatinine from the dashboard figure for every lab in it. The Reference stored with each lab result comes from process-results.ts:550 and :586.

## Not verified
- **Equation coefficients.** I took the CKD-EPI 2021 and 2012 coefficients from the NKF pages on kidney.org. The NEJM and PMC full texts returned 403 or a CAPTCHA. The PMIDs and DOIs were checked on PubMed and Europe PMC.
- **eGFR rounding.** Rounding the lab eGFR to a whole number is my assumption. Labs that print ">90" were not modelled.
- **Live database.** That a `cystatin_c` row exists in the live `biomarker_references` table is inferred from the migrations; the database was not queried. How many clients have cystatin C stored is unknown.
- **Creatine excess (finding 8).** This assumes EVA's own offset is the true creatine effect.
- **Library metadata.** The NHANES cycles and n for cystatin C, and the Comas 2010 slope of 0.8089, were read from the JSON files only, not checked against their sources.

# Cystatin C in KDM v2.2.2: what the published evidence says about the fix options

I read the sources through Europe PMC, PubMed and NCBI E-utilities, the CDC's NHANES documentation pages, the KDIGO 2024 guideline PDF from kdigo.org, and the BioAge README on GitHub.

**How each claim is marked**
- **[V-full]**: I read the full text.
- **[V-abs]**: I read the abstract only.
- **[V-doc]**: I read the official document (CDC page, KDIGO PDF or GitHub README).
- **[V-sec]**: I confirmed it only through a secondary source that I read.

1. **The Spanish cystatin C source is cited under the wrong authors.**

"Cystatin C and cardiovascular risk in the general population." Rev Esp Cardiol 2010;63(4):415-422. PMID 20334807, DOI 10.1016/s0300-8932(10)70062-2. I checked both the PubMed record and the publisher's page [V-abs, V-doc].
   - Europe PMC returns nothing for "Comas MJ" with cystatin C.
2. **NHANES cycles.**
   - The CDC laboratory data-file listings show cystatin C only in these files:

3. **The Reference version still has a kidney filtration marker when cystatin C is present.** BUN is in the base panel, and its KDM weight is 6.0 times that of creatinine in men [Calc §1]. With cystatin C present, the Reference version loses creatinine and does not use cystatin C, but it keeps BUN.
4. **In the Comprehensive version, creatinine still enters through eGFR.**

   - The laboratory's creatinine-based eGFR ("TFGe", mapped in `kdm-adapter.ts:133-135`) stays in, and the creatine offset is not applied to it (`biological-age-kdm.ts:786-793`) [Code].
   - eGFR's KDM weight, (k/s)², is 2.75e-3. That is 25.7 times creatinine's (men) and 17 times cystatin C's [Calc §1]. When a laboratory reports eGFR, creatinine's information still dominates the kidney signal.
5. **The code comment is contradicted by the guideline.** The comment says cystatin C is "the strictly better kidney-aging biomarker" (`biological-age-kdm.ts:765-767`) [Code]. ## 2. Cystatin C versus creatinine for ageing and mortality

**Mortality**
- **Shlipak 2005, NEJM** (Cardiovascular Health Study, n=4,637). PMID 15901858, DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa043161 [V-abs].
  - Cystatin C has a dose-response link with death: the top sixth versus the first quintile has HR 2.58.
  - Creatinine's link is J-shaped.
  - The highest cystatin C quintile carries cardiovascular-death HR 2.27; the highest creatinine quintile is not independently associated.
  - The abstract also says cystatin C "appears to be independent of age, sex, and lean muscle mass". Later work contradicts this for age and sex.
- **Shlipak 2013, NEJM** (11 general-population cohorts, n=90,750). PMID 24004120, DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa1214234 [V-abs].
  - Net reclassification improvement for death is 0.23 when cystatin C is used instead of creatinine.
  - eGFR below 60 is more common with cystatin C (13.7% versus 9.7%).
- **Luo 2015, meta-analysis** (9 studies, n=38,854). PMID 26192218 [V-abs].
  - All-cause mortality HR is 1.32 per SD of cystatin C.
- **Estrella 2025, JAMA**. PMID 41202182 [V-abs].
  - In 11% of outpatients, cystatin C eGFR is at least 30% lower than creatinine eGFR; this group has a mortality HR of 1.69.
- **Wang 2024, NHANES 1999-2004** (Siemens Dimension Vista cystatin C, n=12,914). PMID 39567886 [V-full].
  - A higher creatinine-to-cystatin C ratio (a muscle-mass signal) is protective: top versus bottom quartile HR 0.40.

**Correlation with age**
- **HRS, ages 56-90** (Crimmins 2021) [V-full]:
  - r with age: cystatin C 0.39, creatinine 0.20, BUN 0.25.
  - Cystatin C and creatinine correlate at 0.72.
- **Odden 2010**, healthy participants, n=18,253. PMID 19749145 [V-abs].
  - The age association is strong and non-linear: mean cystatin C is 0.72 mg/L under 40 and 1.06 mg/L at 80 and over (+46%).
- **Köttgen 2008**, NHANES III. PMID 18295054 [V-abs].
  - Cystatin C above 1.12 mg/L: 1% under 20, 41% at 60 and over, more than 50% at 80 and over.
- **European Kidney Function Consortium (EKFC) cystatin C equation**, Pottel 2023 NEJM, 227,643 Swedish patients. PMID 36720134 [V-abs].
  - The median (Q value) is 0.83 mg/L below age 50, then 0.83 + 0.005 × (age − 50).
- **Pottel 2024 review**. PMID 37909162 [V-full].
  - Cystatin C is stable from 18 to 50 (about 0.79 mg/L in women, 0.86 in men), then "increase[s] more rapidly than creatinine".
  - It appears independent of muscle mass.
- **EVA's own fits** [Code]:
  - Path B creatinine: r² 0.019 (men), 0.030 (women).
  - Path B cystatin C: r² 0.027, against 0.103 in the library's original fit (`marker_library_v2_2.json:4207`, `path_b_overrides.json:760-770`).

## 3. What else moves each marker besides kidney filtration

**Creatinine**
- **Muscle mass:** creatinine tracks lean mass; cystatin C does not. Baxmann 2008, PMID 18235143 [V-abs].
- **Cooked meat:** creatinine rose from 80.5 to 101 µmol/L one to two hours after a cooked-meat meal, and eGFR fell from 84 to 59.5. Cystatin C was not affected. Preiss 2007, PMID 17270090 [V-abs].
- **Thyroid:** thyroid dysfunction moves creatinine and cystatin C in opposite directions. Fricker 2003, PMID 12675875 [V-abs].
- **Creatine supplementation**, trials that measured both markers:
  - Gualano 2008, randomised trial, n=18, about 10 g/day for 3 months with aerobic training (PMID 18188581) [V-abs]. Cystatin C fell in both arms: creatine 0.82 to 0.71 mg/L, placebo 0.88 to 0.75. Creatinine fell with training on placebo but stayed flat on creatine.
  - Bender 2008, Parkinson's disease, n=60, 4 g/day for 2 years (PMID 19083405) [V-abs]. Creatinine rose; cystatin C stayed normal.
  - Both trials are listed in Longobardi 2023, PMID 36986197 [V-full].
- **Recent creatine data without cystatin C:**
  - Chun 2026, 10 g/day for 12 weeks, ages 45-65 (PMID 42578920) [V-full]. Creatinine rose 6-8% (under 0.1 mg/dL); creatinine eGFR fell 5-7%, or 14-20% with exercise and diet. Cystatin C was not measured.
  - Naeini 2025, meta-analysis of 12 studies (PMID 41199218) [V-full]. Creatinine mean difference 0.07. The abstract gives the unit as µmol/L; mg/dL is more likely [U]. GFR was unchanged.
- **EVA's creatine offset** (`supplements.ts:147-162`) [Code] gives 0.30 mg/dL at 10 g/day. That is larger than the effects observed in these trials [U, my inference].
- **KDIGO 2024, Table 8** (page S152) [V-doc]:
  - "High-protein diets and creatine supplements" are listed as non-GFR determinants of creatinine.
  - For extreme sport or bodybuilding, cystatin C eGFR "may be appropriate if an increase in muscle mass is the only abnormality".

**Cystatin C**
- **Knight 2004** (n=8,058). PMID 15086483 [V-abs].
  - At the same measured creatinine clearance, these go with higher cystatin C: older age, male sex, greater weight and height, current smoking, higher CRP.
  - It found no evidence that cystatin C-based estimates beat creatinine-based ones.
- **Stevens 2009.** PMID 19119287 [V-abs].
  - At the same measured GFR: diabetes +8.5% cystatin C (and −3.9% creatinine); higher CRP and white cell count and lower albumin also raise cystatin C.
- **Thyroid:**
  - Fricker 2003 [V-abs]: hypothyroid patients went from 0.84 to 1.10 mg/L once treated; hyperthyroid patients from 1.32 to 0.95.
  - Manetti 2005, PMID 15966508 [V-abs], confirms the pattern.
- **Obesity:** adipose tissue secretes cystatin C, and levels are higher in obesity independent of eGFR. Naour 2009, PMID 19360013 [V-abs].
- **Glucocorticoids:** KDIGO 2024 page S181 [V-doc] lists "higher adiposity, smoking, hypo- and hyperthyroidism, glucocorticoid excess, and chronic inflammation". Risch 2001 (PMID 11673383) and Bökenkamp 2002 (PMID 12089191) have no abstract on record, so I could not confirm their direction of effect [U].

## 4. CKD-EPI 2021 and KDIGO 2024

**CKD-EPI 2021**, Inker 2021 NEJM. PMID 34554658, DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa2102953 [V-full, author manuscript].
- The race-free creatinine-cystatin C equation:
  `135 × min(Scr/κ,1)^α × max(Scr/κ,1)^−0.544 × min(Scys/0.8,1)^−0.323 × max(Scys/0.8,1)^−0.778 × 0.9961^Age × 0.963 [if female]`
  with α = −0.219 (women) or −0.144 (men), and κ = 0.7 (women) or 0.9 (men).
- The creatinine-only 2021 equation has an age factor of 0.9938^Age.
- Share of eGFR within 30% of measured GFR (validation, non-Black participants):

  | Equation | Within 30% |
  |---|---|
  | creatinine only | 86.5% |
  | cystatin C only (2012) | 88.9% |
  | creatinine plus cystatin C | 90.8% |

**KDIGO 2024.** PMID 38490803, DOI 10.1016/j.kint.2023.10.018 [V-doc].
- **Recommendation 1.2.2.1 (grade 1C):** use creatinine-plus-cystatin C eGFR "when eGFRcr is less accurate and GFR affects clinical decision-making".
- **Figure 11:** creatinine eGFR is the initial test. Cystatin C eGFR or the combined eGFR can be the initial test "in otherwise healthy populations with changes in creatinine generation" (page S151).
- **Table 11:** "When cystatin C is measured, measure creatinine on the same sample." Cystatin C should be calibrated to the international reference, with desirable bias under 3.2% and CV under 2.0% (page S153).
- **Page S183:** "The combination ... is more accurate ... because the non-GFR determinants for each marker are different." Cystatin C eGFR alone should be limited to people who are otherwise healthy with known changes in creatinine's non-GFR determinants. In 25-30% of people the two markers disagree, and then the combined eGFR is the most accurate.
- **European laboratories:** the EFLM recommends the EKFC equations, combined eGFR, and calibration traceable to reference material. Cavalier 2025, PMID 39584585 [V-abs].

## 5. The KDM independence assumption

- **Klemera and Doubal 2006.** PMID 16318865, DOI 10.1016/j.mad.2005.10.004. I read the abstract only; the full text is closed, so the exact wording of the independence assumption is [U].
- **Secondary sources that state it:**
  - Sluiskes 2024: KDM "assumes that all included markers are functionally uncorrelated", and is therefore used in low-dimensional settings or after principal components. It also shows that the assumption that markers tied to age are tied to ageing cannot be tested cross-sectionally. PMID 38459475, DOI 10.1186/s12874-024-02181-x [V-full].
  - Chan 2021 [V-full] and Cho 2010 (KDM on uncorrelated principal components gave the most reliable estimates; PMID 20005245) [V-abs].
- **The formula** (verified in the Peng 2023 full text): BA_E = Σ(x_j − q_j)·k_j/s_j² / Σ(k_j/s_j)². This inverse-variance pooling assumes each marker is independent evidence.
- **Effect of correlated kidney markers** [Calc §8]:
  - With creatinine and cystatin C correlated at r=0.51-0.72, KDM understates the variance of the kidney estimate by 1.5 to 1.7 times.
  - With creatinine and eGFR, it understates it by 1.4 times.
  - Correlated markers over-weight the kidney dimension and reduce the shrinkage toward chronological age.
- **eGFR has age built in.**
  - The CKD-EPI 2021 creatinine age factor alone produces −0.62 mL/min/1.73m² per year at eGFR 100. That is 74% of EVA's eGFR slope (k = −0.842) [Calc §4]. This assumes laboratories report CKD-EPI 2021; which version Spanish laboratories use is [U].
  - eGFR's per-marker spread on the age scale (s/|k|) is 19.1 years, against 96.8 years for creatinine [Calc §8]. eGFR's apparent precision as an age marker comes largely from chronological age written into the formula [U, my inference].

## 6. NHANES cystatin C

**What the CDC documents** [V-doc]
- **SSCYST_A and SSCYST_B (1999-2002):**
  - Sample: everyone aged 60 and over, a 25% random sample aged 12-59, plus everyone aged 12-59 with high creatinine. Weight variable: WTSCY4YR.
  - Assay: Dade Behring N Latex (particle-enhanced nephelometry) on the BN II.
  - Values: 2,471 and 2,792 participants.
  - In April 2022 the CDC removed some records: 5-10% in 1999-2000, under 5% in 2001-2002.
- **SSCARD_A (stored sera 1999-2004):** measured 2018-2020 on the Siemens Dimension Vista 1500. The documentation says nothing about calibration or traceability to the reference material.
- **NHANES III note:** "Cystatin C calibration has varied substantially across laboratories" between 2006 and 2009.

**Calibration**
- **Selvin 2013.** PMID 23177702, DOI 10.1053/j.ajkd.2012.09.013 [V-full].
  - The 1999-2002 samples were measured in late 2006 at the Cleveland Clinic. In 2009 the University of Minnesota re-measured stored samples from each cycle, and the 1999-2002 values read 0.12 mg/L lower than the Cleveland Clinic results.
  - Recommended conversion: IFCC-standardised value = 1.12 × (reported − 0.12).
  - Cystatin C "changed by as much as 20%" between laboratories; creatinine did not drift.
  - In the 1999-2002 calibration sample the standard deviation was 0.57 mg/L.
- **Inker 2011.** PMID 21855190 [V-full].
  - The ERM-DA471 reference material became available in autumn 2010.
  - The Dade Behring/Siemens nephelometric assay read it about 12% low (standardised value = 1.12 × the Minnesota 2009 value).
- **Foley 2009.** PMID 19339409 [V-abs]: 4,563 adults in 1999-2002, measured in 2006.

**What this means for EVA's n=1,664**
- Path B is unweighted least squares on raw (unwinsorised) values for ages 18 and over (`scripts/generate_path_b_full_overrides.py:26-46, 51-59`) [Code].
- The training data folder is outside the repository (`:21-23`), so I cannot tell which subset gives n=1,664 [U].
- Any unweighted subset of this sample over-represents people aged 60 and over, young people with high creatinine, and kidney-disease outliers. That fits Path B's results: s = 0.543 against 0.298 in the library fit, r² = 0.027, and a KDM weight 0.24 times the library's [Calc §5].
- These are values from before calibration was standardised. The version 3 inventory says cystatin C was "Not converted" (`ml/biological-age/addons/DATA-INVENTORY.md:62`) [Code]. Whether Path B applied the Selvin correction is [U].

## 7. Spanish reference values and assay effects

**Spanish data**
- **Cepeda 2010:** 359 people over 49 (mean age 64, 63.5% women), Aranda de Duero, Dade Behring N Latex nephelometry, measured before the reference material existed. Mean 0.81 ± 0.21 mg/L; manufacturer's normal range 0.51-0.95 mg/L. Diabetes (OR 5.37) and male sex (OR 4.91) predict high values [V-doc].
- **PREDIMED-Plus 2025:** 1,909 Spanish adults aged 65 ± 5 with overweight and metabolic syndrome, Siemens nephelometry. Baseline cystatin C 1.05-1.06 (SD 0.2) mg/L. PMID 39723807 [V-full].
- **García Gallego 2015:** 142 hypertensive patients in Extremadura; top quartile above 1 mg/L; not better than creatinine eGFR. PMID 26051437 [V-abs].
- **Cancho 2024:** controls 0.75 ± 0.13 mg/L, cut-off above 1.03 mg/L. PMID 38388320 [V-abs].
- I found no Spanish population reference-interval study using an assay calibrated to the ERM-DA471 reference material [U, absence in search].

**Assay effects**
- **ERM-DA471 reference material:** certified at 5.48 mg/L. Grubb 2010, PMID 21034257 [V-abs].
- **CAP survey 2014** (healthy pool target 0.960 mg/L): Siemens 0.780, Gentian 0.870, Roche 0.967, Diazyme 1.061; CV 14.3%. Eckfeldt 2015, PMID 25884370 [V-abs].
- **CAP survey 2019:** all-method mean 0.731 against a target of 0.725; CV 9.7%. Karger 2022, PMID 35192685 [V-abs].
- **France and Belgium 2015:** only Siemens reagents on Siemens analysers, and to a lesser degree DiaSys on Cobas, met the minimum criteria. Abbott and Roche had unacceptable bias. Bargnoux 2017, PMID 28188233 [V-abs].
- **Older Siemens platforms:** there is no certified reference measurement procedure, and kits not traceable to the reference were supplied for ADVIA Centaur and Dimension Vista until the end of 2020 (Pottel 2024) [V-full].

**What this means for EVA's cystatin C line** [Code + Calc §2, §6, §7]
- EVA's expected cystatin C is the Spanish q (0.4284) plus Path B k × age. At age 45 that is 0.736 mg/L, 11% below the EKFC median of 0.83.
- A European median value therefore reads as +13.7 years at age 45 and +33.7 years at age 25 on cystatin C alone. The test value of 0.85 mg/L at 45 reads as 61.6 years.
- The 2019 between-method SD (0.071 mg/L) equals 10.4 years on this axis.
- The Spanish factor (×0.81) compares Cepeda's pre-standardisation values with the 2006 Cleveland Clinic measurements, which read 0.12 mg/L high. Part of the "Spanish" difference may be laboratory calibration, not population [U].
- Mixing the Spanish q with Path B's k changes the line by 0.05 mg/L or less between ages 25 and 80, so that mix is not the main problem.

## 8. What this means for the fix options

1. **Option A: apply the cystatin C substitution only in the Comprehensive version.**
   - The Reference version keeps creatinine and the creatine offset whether or not cystatin C is present, and its gate counts only base-panel markers.
   - The literature supports this as the lowest-risk fix:
     - Every standard blood-chemistry KDM (Levine 2013, BioAge, Hastings, Gao, Mak, the original HRS score) uses creatinine, usually together with BUN.
     - KDIGO makes creatinine eGFR the initial test.
   - It makes the Reference figure independent of cystatin C uploaded from other laboratories, whose assays differ by about 10% between methods.
   - Caveat: EVA's creatine offset looks larger than the effects seen in trials.
2. **Option B: one combined kidney marker in the Comprehensive version**, replacing creatinine, cystatin C and the laboratory eGFR. This is what KDIGO's guidance and the decorrelation practice (Chan, Peng, Sluiskes, Cho) point to.
   - It needs a refit using:
     - NHANES 1999-2002 with WTSCY4YR weights and the Selvin calibration, or SSCARD 1999-2004, whose traceability must be checked.
     - Robust handling of the kidney-disease tail.
     - Removal of the equations' age factor.
   - It is the strongest science, but it means retraining and changing client values on a model that is only an interim estimate until version 3. It fits version 3 better.
3. **Option C: take cystatin C out of v2.2 entirely and show it separately** as kidney information with KDIGO context.
   - The cost: cystatin C is one of the strongest mortality markers (Shlipak 2005 and 2013, Luo 2015, Bortz 2023).
   - The case for it: EVA's cystatin C parameters do not hold up.
     - The training sample is unweighted, enriched for older and high-creatinine people, and uses values from before calibration was standardised (r² 0.027).
     - The Spanish q comes from a pre-standardisation sample of 359 people over 49, cited under the wrong authors.
     - A linear fit is applied to an age curve that is flat until 50.
     - Typical European values read 5 to 34 years "older" on cystatin C alone, depending on age.
4. **Needed whichever option is chosen:**
   - Stop the Comprehensive version counting creatinine twice through the laboratory eGFR. eGFR carries 26 times creatinine's weight, gets no creatine correction and has age built in. Peng 2023 dropped eGFR as redundant.
   - Fix the library's citation and its NHANES cycle field.
   - Correct the "strictly better" comment and the methodology wording.
5. **Overall lean:** the literature favours A now, adding the eGFR de-duplication only after it has been validated in staging. B belongs in version 3. C is the conservative fallback if the physician will not countersign the cystatin C parameters.

agents.final_text:
**Recommendation: ship option 1 now.** It puts creatinine back into the lab-page biological age whenever a lab includes cystatin C. It leaves the dashboard figure unchanged whenever creatinine is also present. In the same review, ask the physician one question: do they accept how the dashboard reads cystatin C? If not, follow with option 2. Option 3 is not recommended.

**The problem.** EVA shows two biological ages from one model. The lab-page figure is the Reference version. It is stored with each lab result, shown on the lab page, sent in the results email and read by the AI chat. The dashboard figure is the Comprehensive version. It averages recent labs and uses more markers. When a lab has a cystatin C result, the code deletes creatinine before either figure is calculated. The dashboard then uses cystatin C instead. The lab-page figure uses only base-panel markers, and cystatin C is not one of them. So it ends up with no creatinine and nothing in its place. It also skips the creatine adjustment. The minimum-marker check still counts cystatin C. So a lab-page figure can be published with one marker fewer than the stated minimum.

**Who has it.** Only clients who upload a cystatin C result from another laboratory. EVA's own laboratory does not send cystatin C. On upload, it enters only when someone picks it by hand. The group is probably small. Nobody has counted it, because no database was queried.

**Why option 1.** The lab-page part of the fix is the same in all three options. Option 1 ships it alone, so no dashboard figure moves for clients who also have creatinine. That is the narrowest change to put before a physician. This matters because, in the model-selection decision, the clinical reviewer judged that a physician would not countersign KDM v2.2 at all. Option 1 also fits that decision: keep KDM v2.2 as a labelled estimate until version 3, and fix its claims now. Option 2 can follow later without touching the lab page again. Keeping only today's public disclosure corrects no one's figure. It is acceptable only for the days or weeks the approvals take.

All figures come from seven synthetic test personas run on the live code, not from client data. The personas are:
- a typical man and woman of 45
- a man of 58 on cholesterol treatment
- a muscular athlete of 32 with high creatinine
- a woman of 70
- a man of 52 with metabolic syndrome
- a woman of 38 who is optimal on everything except vitamin D

Ages are in years.

## The three options, ranked

Option 2 ranks above option 3 for two reasons. It removes EVA's weak cystatin C reading instead of stacking it on creatinine. It also moves toward version 3. Option 3 changes the dashboard least, but it counts kidney filtration more than once.

**Option 1, recommended: fix the lab-page figure only.** Candidate A in the working notes.

What it changes:
- The lab-page figure always uses creatinine and never cystatin C. The creatine adjustment applies again to clients with cystatin C.
- The minimum-marker check requires albumin and creatinine. It counts only markers the lab-page figure uses. This is the same check the mortality validation run used.
- The dashboard keeps today's rule: a cystatin C result replaces creatinine. It now ignores a cystatin C value outside EVA's own plausibility bounds. That catches a value typed in the wrong unit.

| Woman on creatine 5 g/day, dashboard | 45.16 | 47.10 | 47.10 | 48.29 | 48.29 |

Who is affected:
- Every lab with a cystatin C result. Its lab-page figure changes when the lab is processed or reprocessed after deploy. It becomes what the same lab gives without cystatin C.
- Creatine users' figures drop the most, because the creatine adjustment now reaches them.
- Real clients can move further than the personas. The size depends on their creatinine. Some clients have creatinine raised by muscle and uploaded cystatin C to show that. They will see a higher lab-page figure.
- The dashboard does not move for clients who also have creatinine and a plausible cystatin C. Two rare cases change. A window with cystatin C but no creatinine now shows no figure. A cystatin C typed in the wrong unit is ignored.

Pros:
- Fixes every confirmed part of the defect. Creatinine is back. The creatine adjustment is back. The minimum-marker check counts only markers in use.
- It is the smallest change clients will see. Typical dashboards do not move, so no dashboard figures are quietly recalculated.
- Removes the absurd dashboard result from a cystatin C typed in the wrong unit.
- Uses the kidney pair of standard blood-chemistry ages: creatinine and urea nitrogen, called BUN. KDIGO 2024 also makes the creatinine-based estimate the initial kidney test.
- Option 2 or 3 can follow without touching the lab page again.

Cons:
- The dashboard still reads cystatin C with EVA's weakest model settings. A value at EVA's own optimal ceiling reads as a much older age.
- The dashboard's swap of creatinine for cystatin C was never validated.
- A laboratory eGFR still counts creatinine twice on the dashboard. eGFR is the kidney filtration rate a laboratory estimates from creatinine.
- The two figures read kidney function from different markers.
- The plausibility check catches most wrong units, but not all. It catches no decimal slips. It has hard edges at its bounds. It checks averaged values, so a window that mixes units can pass.
- Labs with cystatin C but no creatinine lose both figures. A simpler variant keeps their dashboard figure, but it also keeps the wrong-unit result.
- EVA's own creatine adjustment now reaches cystatin C users. The physician must sign off its size.

## Stored results and the methodology page under option 1

**Stored results.**
- Nothing is recalculated at deploy. Labs stored before the fix keep their old lab-page figure. Results emails already sent cannot change.
- Some old labs will change without a separate decision:
  - Editing any value of a lab recalculates it under the new rule.
  - Regenerating the summary of a client's latest lab also recalculates it, when the lab has no master summary.
  - The admin recalculation route rewrites labs too. It must not be run without approval.
  - A recalculated old lab also uses the client's current age.
- New labs get a new method tag, so results under the old and new rules can be told apart. Today every stored figure carries the same tag. The tag name in the draft is a placeholder.
- EVA saves each client's dashboard figure and rebuilds it the next time the client uploads, edits a value or has a lab reprocessed. Under option 1 it comes out the same for clients who also have creatinine and a plausible cystatin C. If the recent labs have cystatin C but no creatinine, the dashboard figure comes out blank. The dashboard then shows the latest stored lab-page figure, which may still be an old-rule value.
- Suggested decision. First, ask someone with database access for a read-only count of labs with cystatin C, and of those without creatinine. Then approve one targeted recalculation of those labs after staging, so a client's history does not mix two rules. The same approval should cover the automatic rewrites above.

**Methodology page.** Today's sentence on the short page becomes false the moment option 1 deploys. The new copy must ship in the same deploy.

| Where | Change |
|---|---|
| Short page, `metodologia/page.tsx:80` in Spanish and `:151` in English | Say that the lab-page figure always uses creatinine and never cystatin C. Say that the dashboard uses a plausible cystatin C in place of creatinine, and still uses a laboratory eGFR. Add a dated line: lab results stored before the fix used the old rule. |
| Full page, `metodologia/completa/page.tsx:127` in Spanish and `:243` in English | Remove "or cystatin C" from the mandatory markers. |
| Counsel note, `METHODOLOGY-CLAIMS-FOR-COUNSEL.md:63-65` | Describe the fix, its date and the stored results. |

Three wording points:
- Do not call the laboratory eGFR "calculated from creatinine". The upload screen also files cystatin-C-based eGFR under that name.
- Do not promise the creatine adjustment to every client yet. Doses written "5 gramos", "5 gr" or "5000 mg" get none today.
- The Spanish text needs review by counsel or a native speaker.

agents.final_text:
**Recommendation: ship option 1 now.** It puts creatinine back into the lab-page biological age whenever a lab includes cystatin C, a blood marker of kidney filtration. The dashboard figure stays the same whenever the lab also has creatinine and a cystatin C inside EVA's plausibility bounds. In the same review, ask the physician whether they accept how the dashboard reads cystatin C. If not, follow with option 2.

Either way, plan the eGFR step. A laboratory's eGFR is the kidney filtration rate that many laboratories estimate and print on their reports. The eGFR step stops the dashboard counting creatinine twice through it. The step first needs a revalidation run, which repeats EVA's test of how well the figure predicts death.

If the physician will not countersign option 1, withhold the lab-page figure for labs with cystatin C instead. Option 3 is not recommended.

EVA shows two biological ages from one model, KDM v2.2. The lab-page figure is the Reference version. It is stored with each lab result, shown on the lab page, sent in the results email and read by the AI chat.

The dashboard figure is the Comprehensive version. It uses more markers. It averages the client's labs from the last 6 months. If there are fewer than two, it uses the last 12 months, or else the latest lab alone. That set of labs is the dashboard's window.

When a lab has a cystatin C result, the code deletes creatinine before either figure is calculated. The dashboard then uses cystatin C instead. The lab-page figure uses only the model's 14 core markers, and cystatin C is not one of them. So the lab-page figure ends up with no creatinine and nothing in its place.

It also skips the creatine adjustment. That is the amount EVA subtracts from creatinine for clients who take creatine. The minimum-marker check still counts cystatin C. So a lab-page figure can be published with one marker fewer than the stated minimum.

Only clients who upload a cystatin C result from another laboratory are affected. EVA's own laboratory does not send cystatin C. On upload, it enters only when someone picks it by hand. The group is probably small. Nobody has counted it, because no database was queried.

The lab-page part of the fix is the same in all three options. Option 1 ships it alone. The dashboard does not move for clients who also have creatinine and a plausible cystatin C. That is the narrowest change to put before a physician.

This matters because of EVA's model-selection decision. In it, the clinical and regulatory reviewer judged that a physician would not countersign KDM v2.2 at all. Option 1 also fits that decision: keep KDM v2.2 as a labelled estimate until version 3, and fix its claims now. Option 2 can follow later without touching the lab page again.

Going step by step has a cost. Each later step is another approval round and another visible move for these clients. Keeping only today's public disclosure is acceptable only for the days or weeks the approvals take.

All figures come from seven synthetic test personas run on the live code, not from client data. Base Panel means the tests in EVA's standard kit.

The test grid has 336 cases. Each persona is tested on the Base Panel and on a full panel. Each is tested with no cystatin C and at five cystatin C levels. Each is tested with and without a laboratory eGFR, and with and without creatine. 280 of the cases have cystatin C. Ages and changes are in years.

The method tag is the label stored with each lab-page figure that names the rule behind it.

No option fully matches version 3. Version 3 ignores results from other laboratories, and cystatin C only ever arrives from one. It also has no creatine adjustment. So creatine users who upload cystatin C will see their lab-page figure drop now. It will change again when version 3 launches, whichever option is chosen.

## The three options, ranked

Option 1 ranks first because it changes the least: no dashboard figure moves in the 336 grid cases. Option 2 ranks above option 3. Option 2 removes EVA's weakest kidney reading instead of adding it next to creatinine.

Option 3 moves the dashboard less than option 2. But it adds one more correlated kidney marker to a model that treats every marker as separate evidence. All three options keep BUN. Options 1 and 3, and step 1 of option 2, also keep a laboratory eGFR on top of creatinine or cystatin C.

All three options change the lab-page figure in the same way:
- It always uses creatinine and never cystatin C.
- The creatine adjustment reaches labs with cystatin C for the first time. It never did before. The deletion and the adjustment arrived in the same commit, and the deletion runs first.
- The minimum-marker check requires albumin and creatinine. It counts only markers the figure uses. This is the check of EVA's mortality validation run. That run tested how well the figure predicts death in NHANES, the US health survey the model was built on.

That shared change carries risks of its own:

| Shared risk | Test result | Suggested handling |
|---|---|---|
| Another laboratory's creatinine returns to the lab-page figure. One common method, uncompensated Jaffe, can read creatinine 30% or more high at low-normal values. Version 3 keeps other laboratories' results out of its age for this reason. It estimates this alone could move its age by up to 3.8 years | A creatinine 30% high would add 2.84 to 3.81 years to the lab page across the seven personas. This is an upper estimate | Uploads without cystatin C already carry this risk today. The broader fix is a separate decision, listed under other routes |
| A creatinine value in µmol/L entered without its unit is read as mg/dL. The deletion used to hide this for labs with cystatin C | Man 45, creatinine 88, cystatin C 0.85: lab page 52.34 today and 898.54 under every option. Dashboard 47.90 under option 1, 400.94 under option 2 and 392.91 under option 3 | Add a creatinine plausibility check, listed under related issues |
| The creatine adjustment can push creatinine down to zero | Woman 70, creatinine 0.35, creatine 20 g/day, cystatin C 1.0: lab page 85.59 today and 73.29 under every option | The physician signs off the adjustment's size |
| Labs with cystatin C but no creatinine lose their lab-page figure | Man 45: 52.34 today, none after | Count these labs before the change |
| Creatine users who upload cystatin C will see a second change at version 3 | See the note under the main table | Say so in the client notice |

**Option 1, recommended: fix the lab-page figure only.**

What it changes:
- The lab page changes as described above.
- The dashboard keeps today's rule: a cystatin C result replaces creatinine.
- The dashboard now ignores a cystatin C value outside EVA's own plausibility bounds of 0.2 to 8.0 mg/L. That catches most values typed in the wrong unit.

Who is affected:
- Every lab with a cystatin C result. Its lab-page figure changes when the lab is processed or reprocessed after the change. It becomes what the same lab gives without cystatin C.
- Creatine users' lab-page figures drop the most. The creatine adjustment now applies to them for the first time. That is why the physician must sign it.
- Real clients can move further than the personas. The size depends on their creatinine. Some clients have creatinine raised by muscle and uploaded cystatin C to show that. They will see a higher lab-page figure.
- Each affected client's dashboard is rebuilt at their next upload, value edit or reprocessing. It comes out the same for clients who also have creatinine and a plausible cystatin C. Two rare cases change. A cystatin C typed in the wrong unit is ignored. A window with cystatin C but no creatinine gets no dashboard figure. The dashboard then shows the latest lab's stored lab-page figure. That may be an old-rule value, or nothing if that lab was recalculated too.

Pros:
- Fixes every confirmed part of the defect. Creatinine is back. The creatine adjustment now reaches labs with cystatin C. The minimum-marker check counts only markers in use.
- It is the smallest change clients will see. No dashboard figure moves in the 336 grid cases.
- Removes the absurd dashboard result from a cystatin C typed in the wrong unit.
- Uses the kidney pair of standard blood-chemistry ages: creatinine and BUN. KDIGO 2024, the international kidney guideline, also makes the creatinine-based estimate the initial kidney test.
- Option 2 or the eGFR step can follow without touching the lab page again.

Cons:
- The dashboard still reads cystatin C with EVA's weakest model settings. A value at EVA's own optimal ceiling reads as a much older age.
- The dashboard's swap of creatinine for cystatin C was never validated.
- One cystatin C upload removes creatinine and the creatine adjustment from the client's whole dashboard average. Option 1 keeps that. So a creatine user's dashboard still rises by up to 2.11 years when cystatin C 0.85 enters the window. Their lab-page figure now falls.
- A laboratory eGFR still counts creatinine twice on the dashboard.
- The two figures read kidney function from different markers.
- The plausibility check catches wrong units and decimal slips that land outside 0.2 to 8.0 mg/L. It misses slips that stay inside those bounds, as the table shows. It has hard edges at its bounds. It checks averaged values, so a window that mixes units can pass.
- Labs with cystatin C but no creatinine lose both figures.

A simpler variant changes only the lab-page code and leaves today's dashboard code in place. Give it the same plausibility check, and it matches option 1 in all 336 grid cases. It still removes the wrong-unit result. It also keeps today's dashboard figure for labs with cystatin C but no creatinine.

The simpler variant has a cost. The dashboard would keep publishing figures without creatinine, which the validated minimum-marker check does not allow. The two figures would also follow different checks. The physician can choose either.

The eGFR step can follow option 1 on its own if the physician accepts the dashboard's cystatin C reading. It needs the same revalidation run as option 2's step 2. Without eGFR, cystatin C carries more weight on the dashboard, so it moves more figures.

**Option 2: take cystatin C out of both figures, then drop the laboratory eGFR in a second step.**

What it changes:

- Step 2: every client whose uploads include a laboratory eGFR, with or without cystatin C. This group is probably larger, because the upload screen recognises eGFR names automatically. It has not been counted. Figures drop most for very muscular clients.

Pros:
- Removes the cystatin C risks at once: weak model settings, differences between laboratories' cystatin C methods, and wrong units.
- After step 1, cystatin C moves no figure. The one exception is a cystatin-C-based eGFR filed as creatinine eGFR, until the name matching is fixed or step 2 ships. Creatinine from other laboratories keeps its own method differences, as the shared risks show.

Cons:

- Moves the dashboards of cystatin C clients at their next upload, edit or reprocessing. Step 2 moves some eGFR clients by many years.

- The dashboard always uses creatinine. A plausible cystatin C is added next to it. A laboratory eGFR stays.

## Stored results and wording

Nothing is recalculated when the change ships. Labs stored before the fix keep their old lab-page figure. Results emails already sent cannot change. Some old labs and dashboards will still change without a separate decision:

| What happens | What it rewrites | Code |
|---|---|---|
| A value of a lab is edited | That lab, under the new rule | `src/app/api/biomarker-values/[id]/route.ts:203-205`; `src/lib/ai/regenerate-master.ts:102` |
| The summary of a client's latest lab is regenerated | That lab, when it has no master summary | `src/lib/ai/regenerate-master.ts:62` |
| The admin recalculation route runs | Every lab it covers. It must not run without approval | `src/app/api/admin/recalc-metrics/route.ts:56` |
| A client uploads, edits a value or has a lab reprocessed | The client's dashboard figure, from all labs in the window | `process-results.ts:616, :775`; `rolling-average-ba.ts:308-326` |

Every lab recalculation uses today's age in whole years and the client's current supplement list, not those at the draw. It also rewrites the lab's longevity score and grade, its version 3 shadow record and the client's dashboard figure. # How other biological-age models, services and guidelines handle creatinine, creatine and cystatin C

Label: other-models. Date: 30 October 2026. This is research only:
- Nothing in the repository was changed.
- No database, app API route or client data was used.
- Computed numbers come from EVA's synthetic personas and the public NHANES files.
- "V" means verified: I opened the primary source or the company's own page and read the number. "U" means unverified.

## Summary

1. **Every published blood-chemistry age I checked uses creatinine.** This covers PhenoAge and its refits, KDM as in Levine 2013 and BioAge, GOLD and Light BioAge, SevenAge, Mamoshina's clocks and LinAge. None of them adjusts for creatine, muscle mass or diet, and none warns about creatine.
   - Only two UK Biobank models use cystatin C: Chan 2021 and Bortz 2023.
   - In both, cystatin C is the strongest kidney marker.
   - When creatinine and cystatin C are in the same model, higher creatinine goes with *lower* mortality. Creatinine then measures muscle, not kidney function.
2. **No consumer service I checked adjusts its biological age for creatine or drops creatinine for creatine users.**
   - Superpower and Rythm warn about creatine on their creatinine pages, but not in the age itself.
   - InsideTracker's InnerAge uses no kidney marker at all.
   - Generation Lab, NOVOS and Tally are DNA-methylation tests and do not use creatinine.
   - Function Health, Ultrahuman, Thorne and Rythm do not disclose the inputs of their age.
3. **Clinical guidelines keep creatinine as the first test and name creatine as a reason to measure cystatin C.** These are KDIGO 2024, the Spanish 10-society consensus of 2022 (co-signed by SEN and SEQC-ML) and NICE NG203. None of them gives a numeric correction for creatine.
4. **The creatine effect on creatinine is about +0.13 to +0.14 mg/dL on average, with a very wide spread between studies.**
   - Pooled results: +0.13 mg/dL (19 randomised trials) and +0.14 mg/dL (26 randomised trials, I² 94%).
   - There is no consistent dose or duration gradient.
   - Single studies range from no change to +0.4 mg/dL.
   - In adults aged 45–65 taking 10 g/day for 12 weeks, the rise was below 0.1 mg/dL without training and below 0.16 mg/dL with training.
   - Measured filtration was unchanged in 4 trials and cystatin C in 2.
   - Creatinine returns to baseline about 4–6 weeks after stopping.
5. **EVA's dose formula is not supported.** The formula min(0.05 + 0.025 × g/day, 0.40) appears in none of the sources the code cites. It over-corrects at 10–20 g/day, and the cited "Mayer & Mannion 1985" is not in PubMed.
6. **In years, creatinine matters most in version 3.** For EVA's typical persons aged 45 on the Base Panel, each +0.1 mg/dL of creatinine adds:
   - about 1.0 year (man) and 1.3 years (woman) on the lab-page figure;
   - 0.4 and 0.6 years on the dashboard figure;
   - 1.4 and 1.8 years in version 3;
   - 0.9 years in the original PhenoAge.
7. **Muscle and diet also move creatinine.**
   - Muscle: creatinine is about 0.10 mg/dL (men) and 0.05 mg/dL (women) higher at the 90th than at the 10th centile of fat-free mass (NHANES 1999–2004, unweighted).
   - Meat: one cooked-meat meal raises creatinine about 0.23 mg/dL for some hours. Guidelines advise 12 hours without meat before the test.
8. **The CEO's "average gives back the age" check, for the two kidney markers only:**
   - **Creatinine** passes in the safe direction. With EVA's own parameters, an average creatinine reads slightly *younger*, not older. EVA expects 1.08 mg/dL (men) and 0.82 mg/dL (women) at age 45. The NHANES median is 0.96 and 0.72; the European EKFC reference is 0.90 and 0.70.
   - **Cystatin C** fails in the other direction. EVA expects 0.74 mg/L at age 45, against 0.77–0.83 mg/L in NHANES and the EKFC reference.
   - The excess age of the typical personas comes from other markers. With creatinine set exactly to its own expected value, the man of 45 still reads 52.05.
9. **EVA's own laboratory already offers cystatin C.** The Echevarne catalogue lists cystatin C (code CISTC) as an active test, measured by nephelometry from the same serum gel tube as the Base Panel. EVA leaves it unmapped on purpose, so it does not reach the model today. It could be offered as an add-on for creatine users.

## 1. Models and services: how each handles kidney markers and creatine

### Published models

The age is linear in the score, so this is **+9.32 years per mg/dL, about +0.93 years per 0.1 mg/dL**. With the corrected divisor 0.09165 it is 9.17 years per mg/dL | No | None. ### What the evidence shows

- **Dose and loading.** There is no consistent dose-response.
  - 3 g and 5 g/day gave the same rise in Vilar Neto 2020.
  - Loading for up to 1 week averaged +0.12 mg/dL (Naeini 2025).
  - Tsiaras 2026 found no difference between under and over 1 month.
- **Washout.**
  - Creatinine was back to baseline 6 weeks after stopping (Robinson 2000).
  - Muscle creatine was back to baseline 30 days after stopping, in 31 men (Hultman 1996, PMID 8828669).
  - Muscle stores take "4–6 weeks" to return (ISSN position stand 2017, PMC5469049).
- **EVA's offset.** The code cites "Mayer & Mannion 1985; Persky & Brazeau 2001; Banfi & Del Fabbro 2006; ISSN 2017" (`supplements.ts:13, :146`).
  - The formula appears in none of the abstracts I read.
  - No paper by Mayer and Mannion on creatine exists in PubMed; the only match is an unrelated 2017 abstract book (PMID 29035170).
  - At 5 g/day (0.175 mg/dL) the offset is close to the pooled mean.
  - At 10 g/day (0.30) and 20 g/day (0.40) it is 2–4 times what trials show; Chun 2026 found under 0.1 mg/dL at 10 g/day without training.

## 5. What a creatinine rise means in years in EVA's models

These are synthetic persons on the Base Panel, run through the deployed code with no supplements. The script reproduces EVA's published figures: 51.29 and 47.20 for the man, 47.83 and 46.29 for the woman.

| Creatinine rise | Lab page, man / woman | Dashboard, man / woman | Version 3, man / woman | PhenoAge |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| +0.10 mg/dL | +0.97 / +1.26 | +0.41 / +0.64 | +1.39 / +1.82 | +0.93 |
| **+0.13 (pooled creatine effect)** | **+1.27 / +1.64** | +0.53 / +0.84 | **+1.78 / +2.33** | +1.21 |
| +0.20 | +1.95 / +2.52 | +0.81 / +1.29 | +2.65 / +3.44 | +1.86 |
| +0.30 | +2.92 / +3.78 | +1.22 / +1.93 | +3.82 / +4.90 | +2.80 |

All values are years. The athlete of 32 and the woman of 70 give similar results.

- **EVA's offset at 5 g/day when the true rise is the pooled 0.13 mg/dL:** the lab page over-corrects by −0.43 years (man) and −0.56 years (woman).
- **At 5 g/day when the true rise is zero:** −1.70 and −2.20 years.
- **At 10 g/day, against Chun 2026's under 0.1 mg/dL:** an over-correction of at least −1.95 years (man) and −2.52 years (woman). This is a linear extrapolation.

## 6. Does an average kidney value give back the age?

These runs use EVA's deployed parameters on the same Base Panel personas at age 45.

**Creatinine.** EVA expects 1.078 mg/dL (men) and 0.816 mg/dL (women) at age 45. These come from the Spanish q, which uses pooled-sex PESA means "not from" the source (`marker_library_v2_2.json:207, :215, :223`), plus the Path B slope (`path_b_overrides.json:31, :38`; `biological-age-kdm.ts:697-705`).

| Creatinine value | Lab page, man / woman | Version 3, man / woman |
|---|---|---|
| EVA's own expected value | 52.05 / 48.66 | 46.34 / 44.02 |
| NHANES median for ages 40–49 (0.957 / 0.72 mg/dL) | 50.88 / 47.46 | 44.61 / 42.21 |
| EKFC European reference (0.90 / 0.70 mg/dL) | 50.32 / 47.20 | 43.72 / 41.80 |

- So an average creatinine reads about 1.2 years younger on the lab page.
- The excess age of the persona comes from the other markers.
- NHANES median creatinine is almost flat with age: men 0.93–0.96 mg/dL from 20 to 59, then 0.99, 1.06 and 1.13; women 0.70–0.74, then 0.77, 0.83 and 0.91. These are unweighted, non-pregnant adults, 1999–2018, with 1,600–4,300 people per cell. 2011–2018 alone gives the same picture.

**Cystatin C.** EVA expects 0.736 mg/L at age 45, against an NHANES 1999–2002 median of 0.82 (men) and 0.77 (women) and the EKFC reference of 0.83. On the dashboard, the man reads 47.50 at EVA's expected value and 47.82 at the EKFC reference, against 47.20 with no cystatin C. Cystatin C at the population average therefore reads older.

## 7. What this means for EVA's options

**What others do.** Everyone keeps creatinine as the base, and nobody applies a creatine correction to a biological age. The tools that exist elsewhere are:
- switching to cystatin C (KDIGO, the Spanish consensus);
- test preparation: no meat for 12 hours, no hard exercise for 24 hours;
- marker-level warnings (Superpower, Rythm);
- dividing by the healthy-population median, as EKFC does.

Version 3 has the largest creatinine sensitivity and no creatine handling, so the choice matters most there.

| Option | Evidence | Effect and risk | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Warn and instruct** | What Superpower and Rythm do; preparation from KDIGO, NICE and the Spanish consensus | No individual correction. The message can quantify the effect: about +1.3 to +1.6 years on the lab page and +1.8 to +2.3 years in version 3 at the average effect. For a clean reading: stop creatine 4–6 weeks before, or add cystatin C; no cooked meat for 12 hours; no hard exercise for 24 hours | **Do now, for both models.** Minimum |
| **B. Replace the dose formula with a flat offset** of about 0.13 mg/dL for current users of 3 g/day or more, taken in the last 4–6 weeks. Subtract before version 3 takes the logarithm, then apply its clamp | Pooled +0.13 to +0.14 mg/dL; no dose gradient; lower in older or sedentary users | Removes the average bias for the group. Each person keeps an error of about ±0.1–0.2 mg/dL, i.e. ±1–2 years (lab page) or ±1.5–3 years (version 3). Use the supplements recorded with that lab, and fix the dose parser | **Recommended** in place of today's formula; needs the physician's sign-off |
| **C. Use cystatin C instead of creatinine when present, never both.** For version 3, a creatinine equivalent = 0.90 or 0.70 × (cystatin C ÷ the age-specific EKFC reference). This works because EKFC's cystatin C equation has "the same mathematical form" as its creatinine one | Cystatin C is unchanged by creatine, meat and muscle. KDIGO Table 8 and Spanish Table 3 name creatine. With both markers in one model, creatinine flips sign (Bortz, Groothof) | The only per-person fix. Do not reuse EVA's current cystatin C parameters, which read an average value as older. Needs standardised assays and validation with both markers and mortality (UK Biobank). Echevarne can run it from the existing tube; cost unknown | **Build as an optional module and validate first** (my inference, untested) |
| **D. Drop creatinine or impute it for creatine users** | No precedent | The KDM gate requires creatinine (`biological-age-kdm.ts:620`) and version 3 requires all 6 markers, so the value would have to be imputed. Kidney information is lost | Fallback only |

**Suggested path:**
1. Ship A now.
2. Replace the dose formula with B in both models.
3. Offer cystatin C through Echevarne to creatine users, and switch C on only after validation.
4. Separately, on the CEO's "average gives back the age" point: an EKFC-style rule, where the expected value is the healthy-population median for the person's age and sex, makes an average kidney value read its own age by construction.

## Unverified

- Function Health using PhenoAge, and Superpower using a "modified" PhenoAge.
- Tally's method on its own page.
- Aging.AI's input lists.
- Whether the EKFC creatinine Q stays constant across adult ages, and its primary source.
- Light BioAge's creatinine unit.
- Naeini 2025's unit.
- Delanghe 1989's numbers.
- Robinson 2000's actual values.
- Any laboratory other than Echevarne.
- The price of Echevarne's cystatin C test.
- What the NHANES fat-free-mass column is.
- Population-weighted NHANES values: all NHANES figures here are unweighted.

  - /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-eva-health/4e1a7523-c199-547a-904f-d87e53286958/scratchpad/cal/other-models/avg_check.out
