I collected 181 Spanish values into the JSON, but only one population-based Spanish source breaks a marker down by both age group and sex. That source is ENRICA, and it covers only the four lipids. For every other marker there are at best sex-specific means across all ages; for albumin, ALP and ApoB there is no Spanish average at all. **Files** - Rows (181 objects; each has study, PMID/DOI, years, region, sampling, age group, sex, n, statistic, value, unit, spread, value in EVA's unit, assay, table, verification status, local copy): `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-eva-health/4e1a7523-c199-547a-904f-d87e53286958/scratchpad/cal/spanish-averages/spanish_averages.json` - Script that builds the rows: `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-eva-health/4e1a7523-c199-547a-904f-d87e53286958/scratchpad/cal/spanish-averages/scripts/build_json.py` - NHANES cross-check output: `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-eva-health/4e1a7523-c199-547a-904f-d87e53286958/scratchpad/cal/spanish-averages/nhanes_crosscheck_output.txt` (scripts `nhanes_means.py`, `nhanes_sex_means.py`, `ratio_check.py` in the same `scripts` folder) - Verification: 158 rows read from the table itself, 16 computed by me from table subgroup means (marked "derived"), 6 from an abstract only, 1 source whose values I could not see. 15 rows are laboratory reference limits, not averages, flagged `not_an_average`. ## What Spain has, by marker | Marker | Best Spanish data found | Age × sex? | |---|---|---| | Total cholesterol, LDL, HDL, triglycerides | ENRICA 2008–10, national sample of 11,554 adults, survey-weighted means. Table 1 (PMID 22483404), age groups 18–29, 30–44, 45–64, 65+. Example: total cholesterol in men 165.4 / 198.2 / 206.5 / 192.2 mg/dL; HDL in women 58.9 / 58.5 / 60.1 / 58.9 mg/dL | **Yes** | | Creatinine | By sex, all ages only:
• ENRICA 0.97 men / 0.77 women mg/dL, Jaffé method (PMID 29914761)
• CORDELIA pooled cohorts 0.98 / 0.76 (PMID 40353978)
• SIMETAP Madrid primary care 0.958 / 0.751, derived (PMID 39201026)
No IDMS-traceable enzymatic population data | Sex only | | BUN / urea | EPIRCE 2004–08, national random sample aged 20+: urea 37.2 mg/dL, which is BUN 17.35 mg/dL, both sexes together (PMID 20038967) | No | | Uric acid | SIMETAP 5.70 men / 4.39 women mg/dL (derived); EPIRCE 4.9 mg/dL, sexes pooled | Sex only | | HbA1c | PESA bank employees aged 40–54: 5.49% men / 5.36% women. SIMETAP 5.71% / 5.57% (derived). AEGIS Galicia median 5.4% | Sex only | | Fasting glucose | PESA, DARIOS (aged 35–74, age-standardised: 105 men / 97 women mg/dL), CORDELIA, SIMETAP, EPIRCE | Sex only | | hs-CRP | PESA subsample median 1.3 mg/L (n=400, age 56±4, 78% men); AEGIS median 1.4 mg/L ("CRP"; high-sensitivity not stated) | No | | GGT, ALT | PESA subsample medians: GGT 24, ALT 22 U/L. AEGIS gives GGT only within glycan subgroups. La Paz hospital gives upper reference limits only | No | | Ferritin | EPIRCE mean 117.7 ng/mL; Di@bet.es median 60.63 ng/mL. Both sexes together, even though ferritin is modelled separately by sex | No | | Vitamin D | La Rioja people whose doctor ordered the test (2013–15, n=21,490): mean 18.3 ng/mL, men 17.6, women 18.5. Ages 55–74 range 19.4–20.4; 80–85 is 16.7; over 85 is 14.5 (abstract only) | Partial | | TSH | Di@bet.es: mean 2.33, median 2.06 mIU/L (n=3,859, no thyroid disease) | No | | Cystatin C | Oviedo random sample aged 50–98: mean 0.81 mg/L, women 0.80, men 0.84 (PMID 20334807). Older assay that predates the IFCC reference material | ≥50 by sex | | Fructosamine | AEGIS only, medians 262 and 251 µmol/L within two glycan subgroups; no overall value reported | No | **Gaps with no Spanish average:** - **Albumin:** nothing found. - **ALP:** one source exists (Castells Vilella 2025, PMID 38797525; 662,350 lab results from 9 Spanish hospitals, percentile charts by age and sex), but the publisher returned 403, so the values are unverified. - **ApoB:** nothing found. - **ALT:** no population-based average. **Gaps by age:** apart from the ENRICA lipids and the vitamin D abstract, nothing is broken down by age group. Under-40s and over-65s are almost absent. ## The Spanish values behind the current recalibration Line numbers refer to `src/lib/biomarkers/data/marker_library_v2_2.json`. - **PESA Table 1** (accepted manuscript; Santander bank employees in Madrid, aged 40–54, mean 45.8, 2010–14, mean ± SD): - Total cholesterol 201 mg/dL (both sexes) - HDL 44.8 men / 56.3 women mg/dL; these match the library exactly (:1287, :1295) - Triglycerides 95 mg/dL; glucose 90.6 mg/dL; HbA1c 5.44% - The library's pooled slopes (:1198, :1485, :1553, :1616) fit these values. - **Mastrangelo 2025 supplement, Table 1a** (n=400, age 56±4, 78% men, 295 with atherosclerosis, both sexes together): - Uric acid 5.9 ± 1.2 mg/dL (mean) - Medians: creatinine 0.85, GGT 24, hs-CRP 0.13 mg/dL. The table labels GGT "mg/dL"; the values look like U/L. - The library's per-sex values are not in this table: creatinine 1.07 for men (:217), uric acid 5.35 / 4.0 (:376, :384), GGT 40.5 for men (:676), haemoglobin 15.5 / 13.75 (:1986, :1994). The women's creatinine 0.85 (:225) and GGT 24.0 (:689) equal the pooled medians of this mostly male sample. - **hs-CRP:** the slope 0.335 (:1747) matches the Spanish median 1.3 mg/L divided by an NHANES *mean*: unweighted NHANES IV gives 0.316 by that route. A median-to-median ratio would be 0.619. This is an inference. - **Díaz-López 2021:** 18.3 ng/mL, from people who were tested, not a population sample. **Alonso 2025:** TSH median 2.09 mIU/L in 1,629 people selected to have TSH between 0.2 and 5.0. - **Cepeda 2010:** 0.81 mg/L, aged 50–98. The library credits it to "Comas MJ…" (:4238); the actual authors are Cepeda, Tranche-Iparraguirre et al. - **NHANES comparison:** the library's stored NHANES means match the all-ages (20–85) NHANES IV means by sex. For example creatinine 0.998 / 0.768 in the library against 1.007 / 0.767 unweighted. So a Spanish value from one age band is divided by an all-ages NHANES value. Against NHANES aged 40–54, the PESA ratios become: | Marker | Ratio vs NHANES 40–54 | Ratio deployed | |---|---|---| | Total cholesterol | 0.991 | 1.016 | | Triglycerides | 0.688 | 0.744 | | HbA1c | 0.960 | 0.936 | This NHANES file is unweighted and is not EVA's training extract. ## Data-quality flags - **ENRICA creatinine** is Jaffé, and the same paper reports kidney disease in 63.3% of men aged 65+. That may mean creatinine reads high; I did not test it. - **EPIRCE HDL** of 71.6 mg/dL is implausible for a general population. - **SIMETAP** prints women's creatinine as "0.7" with one decimal, so I pooled from the paper's other subgroup split instead. - **ENRICA** excluded triglycerides above 400 mg/dL from the whole analysis, so its triglyceride means are slightly low. ## What this means for the "average gives back the age" test Only the four lipids can be taken directly from Spain by age and sex. For every other marker, a typical Spaniard of a given age would have to be built from an NHANES age slope plus a Spanish sex-specific level, which is an assumption. To fill the gaps properly, the options are: - age-by-sex summaries from ENRICA, Di@bet.es, CORDELIA or AEGIS; - the full text of the ALP paper; - anonymised age-by-sex medians from Echevarne's own results. These would use the same assays as EVA's clients, but they would not be population-based.

agents.final_text:
# NHANES audit (nhanes-audit): does a person with average values get their own age back?

## Short answer

1. **With the deployed parameters, no. Average people read older, mostly because of the Spanish intercepts.** The "Spanish intercepts" are the 17 values in which EVA's model moves a marker's baseline level q to Spanish summary values.
   - Test group: NHANES 1999–2018 adults with all 10 Base Panel tests the model reads (5,065 men, 5,129 women).
   - Lab-page figure (Reference): **+2.50 years (men) and +4.77 years (women)** above chronological age on average.
   - Dashboard figure (Comprehensive): **+1.10 and +2.45 years**.
   - With pure NHANES intercepts instead, the same people average −0.10 and +0.30 (lab page), and −0.04 and +0.16 (dashboard).
   - So the NHANES fit is calibrated on average. The upward shift comes from the Spanish intercepts. On the lab page they add a constant **+2.61 years (men) and +4.47 years (women)** at every age. The fitting itself is not the cause.
2. **The Spanish intercepts do not follow their own cited source.**
   - I opened the cited supplement: Mastrangelo et al. 2025, PMID 40670786, Supplementary Table 1a. It describes 400 PESA participants aged 56 ± 4, 78% men, with both sexes pooled.
   - It gives:
     - creatinine as a median, 0.85 mg/dL;
     - GGT as a median, 24;
     - hs-CRP as 0.13 (0.07–0.32) mg/dL, in the table's median-and-quartiles format;
     - uric acid as a mean, 5.9 mg/dL.
   - The library uses per-sex values that are not in the source: creatinine 1.07 and 0.85, uric acid 5.35 and 4.0, GGT 40.5 and 24.0 (`marker_library_v2_2.json:217,225,376,384,676,689`). It divides them by NHANES all-ages means.
   - I rebuilt the shifts consistently: same statistic, with NHANES restricted to ages 52–60 and weighted 78% men. On the lab page the Spanish shift becomes **+1.43 years (men) and +1.23 years (women)** instead of +2.61 and +4.47.
   - Under that rebuild, the creatinine shift reverses: Spanish creatinine comes out about 8% below NHANES, not 7–11% above. Uric acid in women goes from +2.86 years to −0.37.
3. **"Average" needs a definition.**
   - The model's lines are ordinary least-squares lines, so they pass through means. Most markers are right-skewed.
   - With pure NHANES intercepts, a person at the median of every marker reads **1.5–3.7 years younger** than a person at the mean (lab page, Base Panel).
   - With the deployed parameters, the Spanish shift and the median effect partly cancel. So the median person at ages 45–75 reads close to their age by coincidence: −0.0 to +3.6 years. The mean person reads +2.1 to +6.9.
4. **Lack of fit adds age-specific errors.**
   - All lines are straight. Urea nitrogen (BUN) and albumin are fitted with both sexes pooled. The lines were fitted on ages 30–79 according to `audit/audit_C_klemera_doubal_2006.md:6`; I could not verify that range.
   - BUN carries the most weight in the model. It is flat in young adults and rises steeply after 65.
   - Even with pure NHANES intercepts, people aged 20–29 read +2.7 to +3.1 years old (complete Base Panel).
   - At 45, pooling BUN across sexes adds +1.6 years for men and −1.2 for women (mean profile). Pooling albumin does the opposite: −1.1 and +0.85.
5. **The "typical" personas are not typical.**
   - Their BUN is 15 mg/dL (man) and 13 mg/dL (woman). NHANES medians at ages 43–47 are 13 and 11, so the personas sit at the 68th and 72nd percentiles.
   - BUN alone adds +3.72 and +2.91 years to their lab-page figure.
   - With every value NHANES has set to its median, the man goes from 51.29 to 45.63 and the woman from 47.83 to 46.25.
6. **Version 3 (v3) is centred on average, but a median person reads young, and it is more sensitive to creatinine.**
   - The population average of biological age minus age is 0.00 for each sex on 1999–2006, by construction. On 2015–2018 it is +0.19 (men) and −0.14 (women).
   - A person at the median of every marker reads **0.3–2.3 years younger**. This is because v3's floor values lift people below them, so the average age sits above the age of the average person.
   - Creatinine sensitivity: **+1.45 years per 0.1 mg/dL in men and +1.83 to +1.96 in women**, at ages 35–55.
   - KDM's lab-page figure moves 0.84 to 1.26 years per 0.1 mg/dL. Its dashboard figure moves 0.34 to 0.65.
   - EVA's own 5 g/day creatine estimate (0.175 mg/dL) equals +2.4 years (men) and +3.1 to +3.3 years (women) in v3.
   - When a laboratory eGFR (the kidney filtration estimate laboratories calculate from creatinine) travels with creatinine, the dashboard moves **+3.4 to +5.5 years per 0.1 mg/dL**. At 0.175 mg/dL it moves +5.5 to +8.8 years. This uses an eGFR I computed with CKD-EPI 2009.

## What was done
- **Data.** BioAge `NHANES4.rda` and `NHANES3.rda`. Their SHA-256 hashes match `ml/biological-age/pipeline/data.py`.
  - Inclusion follows the version 3 charter: ages 20–84, top-coded ages and known pregnancies excluded (`data.py:64-70,77`). That leaves 50,356 continuous-NHANES adults.
  - Triglycerides, plasma fasting glucose, insulin and LDL are kept only after 8 to under 24 hours of fasting (`data.py:86`).
  - Units follow `pipeline/units.py` and the adapter (`kdm-adapter.ts:90-268`).
  - For fasting glucose I used BioAge `glucose_fasting` (plasma, 2007–2016). It matches the Path B line: 105.4 against 107.8 mg/dL at 45. Serum glucose reads 98.3.
- **Survey weights were attached reliably.**
  - Sources: CDC DEMO files and the fasting-weight files (LAB10AM, L10AM_B, L10AM_C, GLU_D to GLU_J) from `https://wwwn.cdc.gov/Nchs/Data/Nhanes/Public/{year}/DataFiles/`.
  - All 50,356 participants linked by cycle and SEQN, with matching age and sex.
  - Weights: 2/10 × WTMEC4YR for 1999–2002 and 1/10 × WTMEC2YR afterwards; the equivalent fasting weights. GGT from 2001–2002 (second exam, unweighted) is left out of weighted figures.
  - Unweighted results are the main ones, because the model was fitted unweighted. Weighted results are shown alongside.
- **Model runs.**
  - The production TypeScript ran unchanged: `computeReferenceBA` and `computeComprehensiveBA`, no supplements, default fructosamine rule (fructosamine = 19.97 × HbA1c − 39.4, `biological-age-kdm.ts:546`).
  - The intercept variants use a replica of `computeBa` (`biological-age-kdm.ts:717-744`). It matched production to 0.0 years across 100,712 individual runs and 432 profile runs.
  - An independent Python recomputation of one profile gave the same result: +0.628 years deployed, −1.975 with NHANES intercepts.
  - The Python parameters matched `resolveKdmParams` (`biological-age-kdm.ts:674-711`) exactly, in 567 checks.
- **Variants.**
  - *Deployed*: Path B slope k and spread s; the Spanish intercept where one exists, else the Path B intercept (`:700`).
  - *Pure NHANES*: Path B k, q and s for every marker.
  - *Original q*: the library's pre-Path-B intercept, from which the Spanish rule was built.
- **Panels.**
  - *Base*: the 10 Base Panel tests the model reads (`scripts/base_panel_assessment.ts:47-50`), without ApoB and ALT.
  - *Full*: Base plus HbA1c, fasting glucose, insulin, LDL, bilirubin, lymphocytes %, MCV, RDW, white and red cell counts, and vitamin B12.
  - Variants add cystatin C (1999–2002 only), or an eGFR I computed (CKD-EPI 2009).
  - Left out because the NHANES files lack them: ferritin, vitamin D, TSH, ALT, ApoB, AST, haemoglobin, platelets, eGFR, and measured fructosamine.
- **Sealed waves.**
  - As instructed, the main set includes waves 5–8 (2007–2014). That is version 3's sealed test (`CHARTER.md:64,193`), which already used its two allowed runs (`MODEL-CARD.md:13`). It also contains the add-on programme's unused 2007–2010 sealed test (`addons/REPORT.md:23`).
  - No outcome column was used.
  - Version 3 was run only on waves 1–4 and 9–10 and on NHANES III.
  - The KDM conclusions also hold without waves 5–8 (complete Base Panel): lab page +2.95 (men) and +5.02 (women); pure NHANES +0.35 and +0.55.

# Creatine and cystatin C in EVA's biological age: the options compared

**Label:** creatine-options. **Date:** 30 October 2026.

This is research only:
- Nothing in the repository was changed; `git status` is clean.
- No database, app API route or client data was used.
- Every model figure comes from the production TypeScript, run unchanged on NHANES profiles: `computeReferenceBA`, `computeComprehensiveBA` and `computeBiologicalAgeV3`. A replica used for the gate and parameter variants matched production to 0.0 years (`out/options_runner.out`: maxReplica 0).
- "V" means verified here against the primary source. "U" means unverified.

## Short answer

1. **The problem is large in version 3 and on uploads that carry a laboratory eGFR.**
   - The literature puts the creatine rise at +0.13 mg/dL (5 g/day maintenance) and +0.12 mg/dL (20 g/day, first week). For the NHANES average person aged 30–60, that reads older by:

     | Figure | Men | Women |
     |---|---|---|
     | Lab page (KDM Reference) | +1.27 | +1.64 |
     | Dashboard (KDM Comprehensive) | +0.53 | +0.84 |
     | Version 3 | +1.84 to +1.86 | +2.29 to +2.48 |
     | Dashboard, upload with a laboratory eGFR | +4.6 to +5.8 | +5.7 to +8.0 |

     All values are years, at 5 g/day.
2. **Today's handling is wrong in both directions.**
   - KDM over-corrects. On the lab page it reads −0.44 (men) and −0.57 (women) years at 5 g/day, and −2.73 and −3.53 at 20 g/day.
   - It never touches a laboratory eGFR, so +4.1 to +7.2 years stay on the dashboard.
   - It gives no correction for "5 gramos", "5 gr" or "5000 mg". It reads a bare "5000" as 5,000 g, which hits the 0.40 mg/dL cap.
   - Version 3 has no handling at all.
3. **Best default: C2.** Subtract the pooled trial effect, 0.13 mg/dL, for every declared current user whatever the dose. Do it in both models, before eGFR and version 3's logarithm.
   - The average residual is 0.00 at 5 g/day and −0.10 to −0.21 years at 20 g/day.
   - For one person whose true rise is anywhere from 0 to 0.30 mg/dL, the residual is −1.3 to +2.1 years on the lab page and −2.5 to +3.1 in version 3.
   - For women, a relative form (÷1.13) halves the risk of over-correcting.
4. **Do now (C6 + C1):** a pre-test instruction and a quantified warning. Ask clients to stop creatine 4–6 weeks before the draw, or to declare it, and to avoid cooked meat for 12 hours.
5. **Cystatin C:**
   - **C4 as specified** (eGFR from cystatin C by CKD-EPI 2012, then the CKD-EPI 2021 creatinine equation inverted):
     - In NHANES with cystatin C calibrated to the international (IFCC) standard, it implies a creatinine 13–15% below the measured value in men under 60.
     - The average man of 30 or 45 then reads 1.1–1.5 years younger on the lab page and 2.0–2.6 years younger in version 3.
     - The equations' bend points ("knees") make it fragile: a 5% cystatin C assay bias moves version 3 by up to +2.0 years.
   - **C4c (locally calibrated):** removes the average bias by construction. It still moves individuals by a standard deviation of 2.7–3.1 years in version 3 compared with their own creatinine reading.
   - So cystatin C is an optional add-on, not a default.
6. **C3 (leave creatinine out):** with the deployed KDM parameters, the average person reads +0.85 to +1.71 years older on the lab page. The cause is that EVA's Spanish creatinine baseline makes an average creatinine read young. Withholding creatinine is a fallback only.
7. **C5 (cystatin C as its own marker, recalibrated):** KDM only.
   - Recalibrated, cystatin C gets about 10 times creatinine's weight on the dashboard.
   - A straight line across ages 30–79 misplaces the average person by up to 1.3 years on the dashboard and 1.8 on the lab page.
   - Version 3 cannot use it without a new model.
8. **Only the cystatin C routes (C4, C5) touch high muscle mass without creatine.** C4 removes about two thirds of the muscle effect in men. In NHANES women it does not.

## Ranked view

| Rank | Option | Models | Average residual for a declared user, 5 g/day / 20 g/day (years) | One person (years) | Handles undeclared creatine / muscle | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **C6 + C1**: pause 4–6 weeks or declare; quantified warning | Both | 0 if paused for 4 weeks or more. Otherwise the C1 figures, disclosed | – | No / no | **Ship now** (copy and kit only) |
| 2 | **C2**: subtract 0.13 mg/dL (or ÷1.13), dose-independent | KDM now; version 3 at launch | 0.00 / −0.10 to −0.21 | Lab page −1.27 to +1.66 (men), −1.64 to +2.14 (women). Version 3 −2.12 to +2.37 and −2.45 to +3.12, over a true rise of 0 to 0.30 mg/dL | No / no | **Replace today's formula**, with the eGFR and timing fixes |
| 3 | **C4c**: creatinine implied by cystatin C, calibrated locally | Both | 0 by construction. Literal C4: lab page −1.10 / −1.51 and version 3 −1.98 / −2.64 for men aged 30 / 45 | Standard deviation 2.0–3.2 lab page, 2.5–3.1 version 3 | Yes, if cystatin C is measured / partly, in men | **Optional add-on** after calibration and validation |
| 4 | **C3**: withhold creatinine (KDM) or impute it (version 3) | Both | Lab page +0.85 to +1.71; dashboard +0.32 to +0.82; version 3 +0.09 to +0.66 | Standard deviation 1.7–2.7 lab page, 2.2–3.1 version 3 | No / no | Fallback only |
| 5 | **C5**: cystatin C marker with recalibrated parameters | KDM only | Dashboard −0.80 to +1.27 (average person) | Large: cystatin C dominates the figure | Yes / yes | Not now |
| – | **Today** | KDM only | Lab page −0.44 / −0.57 at 5 g and −2.73 / −3.53 at 20 g (men / women). Version 3 +1.70 to +2.48 | – | No / no | Replace |

Two fixes are needed whichever option ships:
- **Laboratory eGFR on uploads.** For declared users, recompute it from the corrected creatinine, or drop it from the dashboard.
- **Timing.** Use the supplements recorded with each lab, applied per lab before the dashboard averages them, not the latest supplement list.

---

## 1. What the code does today (V)

- **KDM creatine offset:** `min(0.05 + 0.025 × g/day, 0.40)` mg/dL (`src/lib/biomarkers/supplements.ts:156-163`).
  - It is applied only to doses in grams (`:186`). "gramos" and "gr" are not normalised (`:114-120`), and a bare number defaults to grams (`:62-63`).
  - A test run of the parser (`out/options_results.json`, key `parser`) gave:

    | Dose typed | Offset today (mg/dL) |
    |---|---|
    | "5g", "5 g", "5", "5g/día" | 0.175 |
    | "10 g/day" | 0.30 |
    | "20g" | 0.40 |
    | "5000" (bare) | 0.40 (read as 5,000 g, capped) |
    | "3-5 g" | 0.125 |
    | "5 gramos", "5 gr", "5000 mg", "una cucharada" | 0 |

  - The comment at `:18` claims "loading-phase 0.5–0.6 mg/dL spikes". The loading trials read here do not support it (section 2.2).
- **Cystatin C deletes creatinine and skips the offset** (`biological-age-kdm.ts:777-784`, before `:786-792`).
  - The gate accepts either kidney marker (`:620-634`), and cystatin C counts in creatinine's slot (`:640-658`).
  - The lab page (Reference) uses only base-panel markers (`:674-711`). So with cystatin C present it has no creatinine and nothing in its place.
- **Laboratory eGFR** maps to the trained marker "TFGe (basada en Creatinina)" (`kdm-adapter.ts:133-135`).
  - Path B values: k −0.8417 per year, s 16.06, r² 0.329, n 18,632 (`path_b_overrides.json:727-737`).
  - Its weight (k/s)² is about 26 times creatinine's in men and 16 times in women.
  - No creatine correction touches it.
  - Echevarne sends no eGFR: no line among the 469 rows of `docs/vendor/echevarne/catalogo-2026-08-25.tsv` mentions TFG, MDRD, CKD-EPI, filtrado or glomerular. So only uploads are affected.
- **Which supplements are used:**
  - Processing reads the client's latest context, not the one recorded with the lab (`process-results.ts:518-536, :722-737`).
  - The dashboard applies today's supplements to every lab it averages, from up to 12 months back (`rolling-average-ba.ts:185-198, :265-270`).
  - A per-lab snapshot already exists: `lab_results.patient_context_version_id` (`supabase/migrations/20260515000000_patient_context.sql:108-111`), written by `src/app/api/lab-results/confirm/route.ts:~181`.
- **Version 3:** no supplement code in `biological-age-v3.ts` or `biological-age-v3-adapter.ts` (grep).
  - Creatinine enters as a logarithm with a floor of 0.8 mg/dL (men) and 0.6 (women) (`data/ba_v3_model.json:92-102`).
  - Its weight is 14.55 years per ln unit in the Base tier (`:439`) and 14.64 with HbA1c (`:219`).
  - The adapter already reads the lab's context snapshot, for pregnancy (`biological-age-v3-adapter.ts:15, :462`).
  - Base Panel tests from other laboratories do not enter the age (`ml/biological-age/PROPOSAL.md:45`). So cystatin C for version 3 would have to come from Echevarne.
  - The add-on programme rejected cystatin C for insufficient data (`ml/biological-age/addons/REPORT.md:16, :32`).
- **Echevarne:** cystatin C (CISTC, I0650) is active.
  - Nephelometry, reference range 0.62–1.11 mg/L, same serum gel tube (`catalogo-2026-08-25.tsv:107`).
  - EVA leaves it unmapped on purpose (`src/lib/lab-provider/echevarne.ts:58`).
  - The catalogue does not state that the assay is IFCC-traceable (U).
- **Patient context fields that C4's exclusions could use** (`src/lib/patient-context/options.ts`):
  - creatine (`:56`), with a free-text dose (`schema.ts:41`);
  - corticosteroid (`:44`);
  - thyroid medicines (`:32-33`) and thyroid conditions (`:85-86`);
  - smoking status (`:129`).

## 2. Inputs

### 2.1 Profiles

The profiles follow the nhanes-audit's "median" method:
- Harrell–Davis medians of NHANES participants aged A−2 to A+2, unweighted.
- Inclusion as in version 3's charter: ages 20–84, below the top-coded age, not pregnant; fasting-only markers kept only after 8–24 hours of fasting.
- 50,356 continuous-NHANES adults are included, the same count as the nhanes-audit.
- At age 45 my medians match the nhanes-audit's exactly, for all 11 markers checked.

Waves:
- KDM runs use waves 1999–2018, as the nhanes-audit did.
- Every version 3 figure uses profiles from waves 1999–2006 and 2015–2018 only. Version 3's charter seals 2007–2014 (`CHARTER.md:64, :193`). No outcome column was used.

Comprehensive (Base Panel) adds ApoB and ALT at the model's own expected values, which add weight but no gap:
- ApoB 95.0–96.7 mg/dL;
- ALT 31.2 / 27.5 / 24.2 U/L for men aged 30 / 45 / 60, and 18.4–19.6 U/L for women.

| | Men 30 | Men 45 | Men 60 | Women 30 | Women 45 | Women 60 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Creatinine, mg/dL, waves 1999–2018 | 0.946 | 0.951 | 0.966 | 0.700 | 0.714 | 0.757 |
| Creatinine, mg/dL, version 3 profile (unsealed waves) | 0.954 | 0.959 | 0.966 | 0.700 | 0.710 | 0.763 |
| Cystatin C, IFCC, weighted median, ages A±5, 1999–2002 (mg/L) | 0.765 | 0.795 | 0.907 | 0.729 | 0.728 | 0.862 |
| n for cystatin C | 183 | 228 | 478 | 161 | 193 | 466 |
| Baseline biological age minus age, lab page | +2.88 | +1.12 | −1.17 | +3.38 | +1.02 | +2.81 |
| Same, dashboard (Base Panel) | +1.20 | +0.47 | −0.49 | +1.72 | +0.52 | +1.44 |
| Same, version 3 Base | −0.75 | −0.46 | −1.48 | −1.56 | −1.24 | −0.87 |

The baseline rows are the nhanes-audit's calibration problem. The residuals below are measured against them, so they isolate the creatine handling.

**Cystatin C data (V).** CDC SSCYST_A and SSCYST_B were downloaded and linked by participant number (SEQN).
- BioAge's `cyst` equals the CDC's uncalibrated SSCYPC exactly (maximum difference 0.0).
- 266 BioAge values are no longer in the CDC release, which removed records in 2021–2022.
- The subsample took everyone aged 60 or over, 25% of those aged 12–59, and every person aged 12–59 with high creatinine (CDC SSCYST_A documentation). So all cystatin C statistics here use the CDC weight WTSCY4YR.
- Calibration to the IFCC standard: `1.12 × (NHANES value − 0.12)`. Source: Selvin 2013, Am J Kidney Dis 61:353-4, PMID 23177702, Table (V). The authors note the same assay drifted "by as much as 20%".

### 2.2 How much creatine raises creatinine: the literature, not EVA's estimate (V)

- **5 g/day maintenance:** +0.13 mg/dL (95% CI 0.07–0.18; 19 randomised trials). Tsiaras 2026, J Ren Nutr, PMID 42035842.
  - No difference between under and over 1 month (P = .15).
  - de Souza Almeida 2026 (PMID 42507286): +0.14 mg/dL (0.05–0.22), I² 93.9%. Measured GFR by Cr-EDTA was unchanged (+5.89 mL/min, −0.30 to 12.08).
- **20 g/day loading, first week:** +0.12 mg/dL (95% CI 0.03–0.21). Naeini 2025, BMC Nephrol, PMID 41199218, subgroup with follow-up of 1 week or less.
  - The unit is printed as µmol/L and is read here as mg/dL (U).
  - Single loading trials: Mihic 2000 (PMID 10694109; 15 men and 15 women, 20 g/day for 5 days) and Poortmans 1997 (PMID 9404870) found no change. Armentano 2007 (PMID 17436778) found a significant rise. Volek 2001 (PMID 11445756) found a rise within the normal range.
- **Smaller or no rise in some groups:**
  - Chun 2026 (PMID 42578920; adults aged 45–65, 10 g/day for 12 weeks): "6%–8% or <0.1 mg/dL" without training (full text).
  - Garcia 2025 (PMC12673977; 71 women footballers, single arm): 0.90 → 0.95 (week 16) → 0.89 mg/dL (week 32) (table).
  - The range for one person used below, 0 to 0.30 mg/dL, takes its upper end from the other-models report (U).
- **Washout:**
  - Hultman 1996 (PMID 8828669; 31 men): muscle creatine was back to baseline 30 days after stopping, and urinary creatinine stayed raised meanwhile.
  - Robinson 2000 (PMID 10953902): serum creatinine "returned to baseline six weeks after the cessation".
  - ISSN 2017 (PMID 28615996): "4–6 weeks".
- **Kidney function is unaffected:**
  - Gualano 2008 (PMID 18188581): cystatin C fell in both arms (creatine 0.82 → 0.71 mg/L).
  - Bender 2008 (PMID 19083405): cystatin C stayed normal over 2 years.

### 2.3 Years per +0.1 mg/dL creatinine (profiles; `out/tables.txt`)

| Figure | Men | Women |
|---|---|---|
| Lab page | +0.97 | +1.26 |
| Dashboard, Base Panel | +0.41 | +0.64 |
| Dashboard, full panel | +0.34 | +0.55 |
| Dashboard + laboratory eGFR (CKD-EPI 2009 from the measured creatinine) | +3.64 to +4.61 | +4.52 to +6.36 |
| Version 3 Base | +1.43 to +1.45 | +1.79 to +1.94 |

Version 3 Base + HbA1c is within 0.02 of Base.

### 2.4 Equations used for C4 (V)

- **CKD-EPI 2012 cystatin C** (Inker 2012, NEJM 367:20-29, PMID 22762315, Table 2; the same equation appears in the Spanish consensus, García-Maset 2022, DOI 10.1016/j.nefro.2021.07.010, Tabla 2):
  - `eGFRcys = 133 × min(Scys/0.8,1)^−0.499 × max(Scys/0.8,1)^−1.328 × 0.996^age × 0.932 [women]`
  - Scys must be traceable to IFCC/ERM-DA471. Both papers say so, and the consensus says the equations are "solo válidas para métodos … estandarizados" (valid only for standardised methods).
- **CKD-EPI 2021 creatinine, inverted** (Inker 2021, NEJM 385:1737-49, PMID 34554658, Table 1: 142; κ 0.7 women / 0.9 men; α −0.241 / −0.302; −1.200; 0.9938^age; ×1.012 women):
  - `C = eGFRcys / (142 × 0.9938^age × 1.012 [women])`
  - `Scr = κ × C^(1/α)` if C ≥ 1, otherwise `Scr = κ × C^(−1/1.200)`
  - Example: a man of 45 with cystatin C 0.795 mg/L has eGFRcys 111.4, which implies creatinine 0.796 mg/dL. His median measured creatinine is 0.951.
- **Sensitivity of the map.** How much implied creatinine changes for a given change in cystatin C depends on where the person sits:

  | Position | Implied creatinine change per 1% cystatin C change |
  |---|---|
  | Above both knees | 1.1% |
  | Both below the knees | 1.7% (men), 2.1% (women) |
  | Cystatin C above, creatinine below its knee | 4.4% (men), 5.5% (women) |

  Typical young and middle-aged men sit near both knees.

| Version 3, women | 0 to +5.13 | 0 to +5.13 | 0 to +5.13 | −2.45 to +3.12 |

The version 3 C2 lower end for women includes the 0.6 mg/dL floor.

## 4. The options in turn

### C1: warn only

- **What it does:** the model is unchanged. Declared users are told the effect in years.
- **With cystatin C:** today's deletion rule still applies (section 5). Version 3 keeps the full effect.
- **Failure modes:** undeclared users get no warning. The number stays biased by +1.2 to +1.6 years (lab page) and +1.7 to +2.5 (version 3), and by up to +8 on eGFR uploads. It does not address muscle.
- **Data and code:** the creatine flag from the lab's context snapshot, and copy for the lab page, results email, AI chat and methodology page. The page currently says EVA subtracts a dose-based amount (`metodologia/page.tsx:79`).
- **Physician signs:** the wording and the numbers.

### C2: an evidence-based offset

- **What it does:** replace `creatineCreatinineOffsetMgDL` with a flat 0.13 mg/dL. Apply it:
  - for any declared current use (at least about 3 g/day, or a loading week) at the draw;
  - before eGFR is computed, and before version 3's logarithm and floor.
- **Absolute or relative?**
  - In men the two forms differ by less than 0.1 year.
  - For women the evidence is thin. If the true rise is relative (+13%), the absolute form over-corrects by −0.40 to −0.49 on the lab page and −0.60 to −0.83 in version 3. If it is absolute, the relative form under-corrects by +0.35 to +0.43 and +0.51 to +0.70.
  - At Garcia's +0.05 mg/dL in women: absolute −1.01 / −1.61 to −1.77; relative −0.46 to −0.54 / −0.77 to −0.85.
  - Recommendation: ÷1.13, as the physician chooses.
- **With cystatin C:** for KDM there is nothing to correct while the deletion rule stands. If the CYSTATIN-C-FIX option 1 or 2 restores creatinine on the lab page, C2 applies there. Version 3 always applies it.
- **Failure modes:**
  - Undeclared use: equals C1.
  - Declared but stopped 2 weeks ago: lab page −0.63 / −0.82, version 3 −1.0 / −1.4. So ask for the stop date: no offset if stopped 4 weeks or more.
  - Dose typos stop mattering, because the offset ignores the dose.
  - Creatinine typed in µmol/L is absurd in every option (+65 years in version 3); a plausibility check is needed.
  - Muscle: not addressed.
- **Data and code:**
  - `supplements.ts:156-190` and the parser;
  - the per-lab snapshot instead of the latest list (`process-results.ts:523-536, :726-737`);
  - adjust per lab before averaging (`rolling-average-ba.ts:159-183, :265-270`);
  - recompute or drop "TFGe" for declared users;
  - a version 3 adapter hook that records the adjustment in `bio_age_v3_shadow`.
- **Client message:** see section 8.

### C3: leave creatinine out

- **KDM:** the gate must accept "creatinine withheld for creatine".
  - Today albumin plus creatinine or cystatin C is mandatory (`biological-age-kdm.ts:620-634`), and the mortality validation requires creatinine (`scripts/comprehensive_ba_mortality_validation.py:47`). So this runs outside the validated configuration.
  - The Base Panel keeps 9 of the 14 base markers, at least the 8 required.
- **Version 3:** impute creatinine as `exp(mean ln(max(creatinine, floor)))` by sex and age. This keeps version 3's population average, because the model is linear in ln creatinine.
  - Values from NHANES 1999–2006: men 0.960 / 0.967 / 0.997; women 0.731 / 0.743 / 0.790 mg/dL at ages 30 / 45 / 60.
- **Residuals:** the KDM numbers in section 3 mostly reflect EVA's own creatinine baseline. With the pure NHANES creatinine baseline (Path B q), the lab-page residual falls to:
  - −0.03 / +0.45 / +0.82 (men) and +0.10 / +0.57 / +0.89 (women);
  - what remains is the straight-line misfit with age.
- **One person:** standard deviation 1.65–2.68 years on the lab page and 2.15–3.08 in version 3.
- **With cystatin C:** today's rule already drops creatinine.
- **Signs:** a figure computed without creatinine, the imputation table, and the labels.

### C4: creatinine implied by cystatin C

**Population check:** NHANES 1999–2002, weighted, IFCC-calibrated; n = 2,023 men and 1,867 women.

| Group | Implied vs measured creatinine, median ln ratio | Version 3 years: median (standard deviation) |
|---|---|---|
| Men 20–39 | −0.135 | −0.99 (2.65) |
| Men 40–59 | −0.146 | −0.99 (2.88) |
| Men 60–84 | +0.016 | +0.24 (3.01) |
| Women 20–39 | −0.054 | −0.15 (2.51) |
| Women 40–59 | −0.074 | −0.35 (2.92) |
| Women 60–84 | +0.048 | +0.64 (2.99) |

- Inverting CKD-EPI 2009 instead of 2021 makes the bias worse: −0.161 / −0.191 for men aged 20–39 / 40–59 (`out/c4_inversion_2009.out`).
- The EKFC-form map is also biased: −0.11 (men) and −0.15 (women). Its reference values are U.
- So any fixed published equation needs local calibration.
- **C4c, calibrated** (typical creatinine × (cystatin C ÷ typical cystatin C)^1.107, from weighted fits on age and age² by sex): median ln ratio −0.02 to +0.005, version 3 standard deviation 2.72–3.05 years.

**Assumption checks:**

1. **IFCC traceability.** It is required, and unconfirmed for Echevarne.
   - A +5% cystatin C bias moves literal C4 by +0.3 to +2.0 years in version 3 and +0.2 to +1.2 on the lab page (isolated effect).
2. **Causes of high cystatin C other than kidney function.** KDIGO 2024 (PMID 38490803, p. S181) lists higher adiposity, smoking, hypo- and hyperthyroidism, glucocorticoid excess and chronic inflammation. The Spanish consensus adds diabetes.
   - **Inflammation:** cystatin C is +0.033 ln per ln CRP in men and +0.014 in women, adjusted for age, creatinine and BMI (NHANES).
     - CRP 10 vs 1 mg/L moves C4 by +1.2 to +2.4 years in version 3 (men) and +0.2 to +0.5 (women), because of the knees.
     - The median calibrated ratio runs from −0.077 at CRP 1 mg/L or less to +0.063 above 10 (men), and from −0.052 to +0.095 (women).
     - Version 3 already contains CRP, so inflammation would count twice.
   - **Thyroid:** Fricker 2003 (PMID 12675875) measured cystatin C at 1.32 mg/L in hyperthyroidism, 0.95 after treatment, and 0.84 → 1.10 in hypothyroidism.
     - Hyperthyroidism gives +4.4 to +6.5 years in version 3 and +3.1 to +4.4 on the lab page.
     - Hypothyroidism gives 0 to −3.6 years in version 3 (floored) and −2.8 to −4.0 on the lab page.
   - **Smoking:** calibrated ratio +0.067 vs −0.050 (men) and +0.108 vs −0.025 (women).
   - **Obesity:** BMI 30 or more vs under 25 gives +0.039 vs −0.057 (men) and +0.055 vs −0.071 (women).
   - **Steroids:** Risch 2001 (PMID 11673383) is verified by title only.
3. **Decimal slip.** 0.795 typed as 7.95 sits inside the bounds file's 0.2–8.0 mg/L (`plausibility_bounds.json:72`, which no code reads).
   - It gives +36 to +38 years in version 3 and +97 to +114 on the lab page.
   - It needs a consistency check between implied and measured creatinine.

**Other points:**
- **Muscle (ages 20–49, weighted):**
  - Men in the top vs bottom third of fat-free mass: measured creatinine 1.000 vs 0.905 (+10.5%), calibrated C4 0.952 vs 0.918 (+3.7%).
  - Women: measured 0.755 vs 0.735, calibrated C4 0.764 vs 0.664 (+15%). Their cystatin C is 0.762 vs 0.683 mg/L, which reflects body size, not muscle.
- **Version 3:** cystatin C must come from Echevarne's same draw (`PROPOSAL.md:45`). Capillary (Tasso) cystatin C is untested (U).
- **Signs:** the map and its calibration data, the assay requirement, the exclusions (thyroid disease or treatment, systemic steroids, hs-CRP above 10 mg/L, BMI of 35 or more), the consistency-check limits, who receives it, and a label saying version 3 runs outside its validation.

### C5: cystatin C as its own marker

- **Recalibrated parameters:** weighted least squares of ln IFCC cystatin C on age, NHANES 1999–2002, ages 30–79 (`out/profiles.json`, key `c5_fits`).

  | | k per year | q | s | r² | n |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | Men | 0.00785 | −0.536 | 0.235 | 0.155 | 1,674 |
  | Women | 0.00904 | −0.654 | 0.249 | 0.193 | 1,532 |

  - Deployed parameters (pooled, linear): k 0.00684, Spanish q 0.4284, s 0.543 (`path_b_overrides.json:760`; `marker_library_v2_2.json:4244`). They expect 0.736 mg/L at 45.
- **Weight:** (k/s)² is about 1.1–1.3 × 10⁻³ against creatinine's 1.1 × 10⁻⁴. So cystatin C would dominate the dashboard: +5% cystatin C gives +0.9 years, and a ×10 slip gives +42 to +43.
- **Average person:** a straight line misses cystatin C's flat-then-rising age curve, so the residuals in section 3 swing by age.
- **Version 3:** impossible without a new model (UK Biobank).
- **Signs:** the new parameters, a revalidation (`docs/runbooks/kdm-panel-revalidation.md`), and a dashboard change for everyone who has cystatin C.

### C6: pre-test instruction

- **What it asks:** stop creatine 4 weeks before the draw, and 6 to be sure (Hultman 1996, Robinson 2000, ISSN 2017). Otherwise declare the dose.
- **Meat:** no cooked meat or fish in the 12 hours before. KDIGO 2024 (p. S182) gives +0.23 mg/dL creatinine and says waiting at least 12 hours "best avoids this effect". Nair 2014 (PMID 24062331): the effect "disappears after 12 h of fasting". Preiss 2007 (PMID 17270090): cystatin C "generally uninfluenced" by food.
- **Exercise:** advice to avoid hard exercise in the previous 24 hours is not verified here (U).
- **Residual:** 0 if followed. A 2-week pause leaves about half the effect, assuming a linear decline over 30 days (U).
- **Limits:** compliance cannot be checked.
- **Data:** the booking or kit flow, and structured fields: taking yes/no, g/day, start date, stop date.
- **Signs:** the instruction, including "unless a doctor prescribed it".

**Which options handle high muscle mass without creatine:** only C4 (always applied, and partly; men only in NHANES) and C5. The muscle effect for the 90th vs 10th centile of fat-free mass, which no declared-creatine option touches:

| Figure | Men (+0.10 mg/dL) | Women (+0.05 mg/dL) |
|---|---|---|
| Lab page | +0.97 | +0.63 |
| Version 3 | +1.43 to +1.46 | +0.93 to +1.00 |

Basis: NHANES 1999–2004, ages 20–49; slope 0.037 mg/dL per 10 kg fat-free mass in men (n 2,507) and 0.025 in women (n 2,371).

## 5. Behaviour with and without cystatin C, and the CEO's "average gives back the age" check

| Option | No cystatin C | Cystatin C present |
|---|---|---|
| Today | Formula offset in KDM; nothing in version 3 | KDM drops creatinine and the offset. The average person, no creatine, reads +0.85 to +1.71 (lab page) and +0.63 to +0.94 (dashboard) |
| C1 / C6 | As described | Same, plus the same cystatin C rule |
| C2 | Offset | KDM: no creatinine to correct unless the deletion rule changes. Version 3: offset |
| C3 | Withhold / impute | KDM dashboard falls back to cystatin C |
| C4 | Not available; fall back to C2 | Average person: literal −1.10 / −1.51 / +0.12 (men, lab page) and −1.98 / −2.64 / +0.18 (version 3). Calibrated (C4c): 0 |
| C5 | Not available | Average person, dashboard: +0.70 / −0.49 / +0.06 (men), +1.27 / −0.80 / −0.22 (women) |

So by the CEO's test, an average value should give back the age:
- The deployed cystatin C fails (reads older).
- Literal C4 fails for men under 60 (reads younger).
- C5 fails by age band.
- Only C4c passes by construction.
- For creatine itself, only C2 makes an average declared user read like their non-creatine self.

## 6. Physician sign-off and work needed (summary)

| Option | Physician signs | Code and data |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | Wording and numbers | Copy; per-lab creatine flag |
| C6 | Instruction (4–6 weeks; meat 12 hours; exceptions) | Kit or booking copy; structured creatine fields |
| C2 | Size and form (0.13 or ÷1.13), eligibility (current use; none if stopped 4 weeks or more), both models, eGFR handling, label, stated uncertainty | `supplements.ts`; per-lab snapshot; per-lab before averaging; eGFR recompute or drop; version 3 adapter hook; tests |
| C3 | Figure without creatinine; version 3 imputation table; label | Gate change (`:620-634`, `:771-795`); version 3 adapter table |
| C4c | Map and calibration, IFCC assay, exclusions, consistency check, label | Map CISTC; calibration on paired data (U: a sample of the order of 1,000); equations; checks |
| C5 | New parameters, revalidation, dashboard change for all with cystatin C | Refit plus revalidation run |

## 7. Recommended sequence

1. **Now, both models:** C6 + C1.
2. **KDM now:** replace the formula with C2, and fix the parser. Use the lab's own snapshot and adjust per lab before averaging. Recompute or drop the laboratory eGFR for declared users; removing it from the dashboard is the separate "eGFR step" in `CYSTATIN-C-FIX-OPTIONS.md`.
3. **Version 3:** add the creatine fields now. Ship C2 at launch with the physician's countersignature.
4. **Cystatin C:** offer Echevarne's test as an add-on for non-pausing creatine users and very muscular clients. Use it (C4c) only after:
   - IFCC traceability is confirmed;
   - the map is calibrated locally;
   - exclusions and a consistency check are in place;
   - and, for version 3, ideally the UK Biobank add-on validation.
5. Hold C3 as a fallback. Do not ship C5.

## 8. Client messages

These drafts need review by counsel; the Spanish needs a native or counsel review.

- **C6 (EN):** "Before your blood test: if you take creatine, stop it 4 to 6 weeks before the draw, unless a doctor prescribed it. If you can't, tell us your daily dose. Don't eat cooked meat or fish in the 12 hours before."
- **C6 (ES):** "Antes de tu analítica: si tomas creatina, déjala 4 a 6 semanas antes de la extracción, salvo que te la haya pautado un médico. Si no puedes, indícanos la dosis diaria. No comas carne ni pescado cocinados en las 12 horas previas."
- **C1 (EN):** "You told us you take creatine. Creatine raises blood creatinine without harming the kidneys: by about 0.13 mg/dL on average in trials. Our model reads creatinine as a sign of ageing, so your biological age may read about 1.3 years older (women: 1.6) on this result than without creatine. For a clean reading, pause creatine 4 to 6 weeks before your next test."
- **C2 (EN):** "Because you take creatine, we lowered your creatinine by the average amount creatine adds (about 0.13 mg/dL) before calculating your biological age. Your own response may differ. Pausing creatine for 4 to 6 weeks before a test gives a reading without this adjustment."
- **C4 (EN):** "Because you take creatine, we estimated your kidney marker from cystatin C, which creatine does not change."

## 9. Not verified

- Echevarne's cystatin C calibration (IFCC traceability) and its price.
- Whether Spanish laboratories report CKD-EPI 2009 or 2021. The consensus's Tabla 2 shows 2009; the version 3 adapter assumes 2021.
- The 0.30 mg/dL upper end of one person's response.
- The rise in women.
- The shape of the washout curve (linear decline assumed).
- Naeini's unit.
- Risch 2001's numbers.
- The content of the Selvin 2013 erratum.
- What the NHANES fat-free-mass column measures.
- Capillary cystatin C.
- How many EVA clients take creatine or upload a laboratory eGFR (no database was queried).
- The advice on exercise in the previous 24 hours.

# Calibration check: does a person with average Spanish values get their own age back? (label: calibration)

## Verdict

**Deployed KDM v2.2.2: no.**
- **Lab page (Reference).** For Spanish average-for-age profiles on the 10 Base Panel tests the KDM reads:
  - −1.0 to +3.7 years in men and −1.2 to +3.2 in women, ages 24–75, if Spanish BUN equals NHANES.
  - A synthetic population moved to Spanish levels reads +1.9 years (men) and +1.4 (women) on average.
- **Dashboard (Comprehensive).** It moves about half as much.
- **BUN.** If Spanish BUN is 29% above NHANES, as the only Spanish population source (EPIRCE) says, the lab page reads +8.0 to +11.5 (men) and +3.7 to +8.3 (women). The deployed model does not adjust BUN at all.
- **Vitamin D, a new bug.** When vitamin D is on the panel, the lab page reads 3.6 to 7.4 years younger than without it.
  - EVA sends ng/mL values (`kdm-adapter.ts:235-236`) into a line fitted on NHANES values in nmol/L, although the library labels it ng/mL (`marker_library_v2_2.json:3434`).
  - Evidence the line is in nmol/L: it runs 0.94–1.02 times the NHANES mean in nmol/L in every 10-year band from 20 to 79, and its residual SD is 27.0 against 26.9 in the nmol/L data. The CDC labels LBXVIDMS "(nmol/L)" in its VID_J codebook (wwwn.cdc.gov/Nchs/Data/Nhanes/Public/2017/DataFiles/VID_J.htm).

**The NHANES fit is not what is wrong.**
- With pure NHANES intercepts, NHANES participants read +0.3 (men) and +0.5 (women) on the lab page.
- The Spanish intercepts add +2.60 (men) and +4.47 (women) years to everyone with the Base Panel.
- About 1.3 and 1.4 of those years have no support in Spanish data. The causes:
  - per-sex values that are not in the cited table;
  - an hs-CRP median compared with an NHANES arithmetic mean;
  - bank employees used as the reference for triglycerides and HDL;
  - an all-ages NHANES mean as the comparison;
  - an intercept that is scaled instead of shifted.

**Version 3: close for the population, about 1 year young for a typical person.**
- The Spanish-level population reads −0.5 (men) and −0.3 (women) on the Base tier, and −0.2 and 0.0 with EPIRCE BUN. The mean in every age band is between −1.1 and −0.1.
- A person with exactly average values reads 0.6 to 1.9 years younger. Version 3 is centred on the average of people, and its floor values lift the people below them.
- Version 3 has no Spanish intercepts, and BUN barely moves it.

**How to fix it.**
1. Fix the vitamin D unit, or drop vitamin D from the KDM.
2. Replace the 17 Spanish intercepts with the corrected rule C1 (JSON below). This removes 1.3 years (men) and 1.4 (women) of excess for an average Spaniard on the lab page, and brings the population average to +0.5 and 0.0.
3. Settle Spanish BUN with data before any other change; it decides about ±7 years on the lab page.
4. Do not try to make the KDM exact. Its straight lines leave errors that no intercept removes:
   - +3.7 years in men aged 20–29;
   - −1.9 to +1.2 in women aged 40–59.
   - Under C1, independent Spanish averages at ages 45–55 return their age within ±1 year for men (−0.6 to +1.0), but not for women (−1.3 to +3.7).
5. For version 3, recentre its two per-sex constants on individual-level Spanish data. The expected size of the change is about 0 to +0.7 years.

The repository was not modified. No database, app API route or patient data was used. NHANES numbers are unweighted, as the model was fitted, from the BioAge file (SHA-checked; ages 20–84; known pregnancy and top-coded ages excluded).

---

## 1. Spanish levels used (Spanish value ÷ NHANES at the source's ages and sex)

| Marker | Source (PMID) | Population | Spanish value | Ratio, men / women |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Creatinine | ENRICA 2008–10 (29914761) | National sample, 5,675 men and 5,830 women, mean age 47, Jaffé method | 0.97 / 0.77 mg/dL | 0.979 / 1.012 |
| Uric acid | SIMETAP (39201026) | Madrid primary care, 2,857 men and 3,632 women, mean age 55; values derived from subgroup means | 5.70 / 4.39 mg/dL | 0.940 / 0.882 |
| Total cholesterol, HDL, triglycerides (TG) | ENRICA (22483404) | National, survey-weighted, 4 age bands by sex | TC 192.9 / 198.8; HDL 47.0 / 59.1; TG 120 / 95.9 mg/dL | TC 0.999 / 1.012; HDL 0.988 / 1.040; TG 0.931 / 0.833 |
| hs-CRP | AEGIS 2012–15 (41106480) | Galicia random sample, n = 1,516, median age 52; the paper says "CRP", high-sensitivity not stated | median 1.4 mg/L | 0.662 |
| GGT | PESA subsample (40670786) | n = 400, 78% men, 75% with atherosclerosis | median 24 U/L | 0.960 (AEGIS subgroups: 1.05, 0.95) |

These rows exclude the table's "line versus data at the source's age" step, so they do not add up to the total. That step is −0.49 / −0.32 for creatinine, +0.40 for uric acid in women and +0.30 / +0.23 for triglycerides; Base Panel totals −0.36 / +0.80.

What each step means:
- **The rule.** The deployed rule multiplies the age-0 intercept by a ratio measured in adults (`fix_spanish_recalibration_bug.py`; methodology page, `metodologia/completa/page.tsx:222`).
  - That shifts the line by (ratio − 1) × q rather than by the gap at adult ages. Its cost is largest for uric acid in women: −1.21 years.
  - The page itself says "only the starting level differs" (`page.tsx:222`), which scaling q does not do.
- **The comparison mean.** The NHANES side is an all-ages mean: 0.998 / 0.768 mg/dL for creatinine, 3.88 mg/L implied for hs-CRP. The Spanish side is a single age group.
- **The log fix.** The 2026-09-25 correction for log-scale markers is right as long as both sides are the same statistic. The remaining log-scale error is statistical: the hs-CRP Spanish median of 1.3 mg/L is divided by an NHANES arithmetic mean, worth +1.19 / +0.93 years.
- **The Path B mix is small**: −0.31 (men) and −0.15 (women) years.
- **The sources.**

The library's own citation blocks say these per-sex means "are not from it", and so does the methodology page (`page.tsx:224`).
  - The lipid source is PESA: bank employees aged 40–54 in Madrid, with triglycerides 30–38% below NHANES against 7–17% in ENRICA.
- **EVA's own documents.**
  - The methodology page sets exactly the CEO's goal: a Spanish user with typical values should not be skewed (`page.tsx:221`). It also discloses +3.5 years on NHANES (`page.tsx:282`).
  - GATE-1 decision BA2 accepted hs-CRP at "one third of the NHANES level" and recorded the risk as 1.6 / 1.1 years (`GATE-1-DECISIONS.md:307-320`).
  - `KDM-EXPLAIN-PANELS.md:15` lists vitamin D at −4.5 years as the typical man's largest contribution. That is the unit error, but the document does not identify it as one.
- **Not intercept problems.** These stay after any intercept fix:
  - BUN level (section 1).
  - Straight lines with pooled sexes. With NHANES q on NHANES mean profiles, men read +3.2 at 25 and women −1.5 at 45 and +1.9 at 55.

## 4. The corrected rule (C1) and its test

- **Rule.** q = T(c) − k_PathB × ā, per sex for sex-stratified markers.
  - c is the Spanish population central value on the model's scale: arithmetic mean for linear markers, geometric mean for log markers. Medians and arithmetic means are converted with the NHANES ratio at the same ages and sex.
  - ā is the source's mean age. T is identity for linear markers and ln for log markers.
  - Pooled-sex KDM markers are set at the training sex mix (49.7% men). Path B k and s are kept.
  - Only traceable, population-based values are used; otherwise the marker gets the NHANES (Path B) q.
- **Test copy.** Tested in scratch copies of `biological-age-kdm.ts` that differ from production only in the 6 import lines. Parity with production was 0 years over 1,564 profile rows and 103,971 population rows. A plain-Python recomputation matched to 1e-4 years.

| Version 3 as frozen | −0.5 / −0.2; −0.3 / 0.0; bands −1.1 to −0.1 | Typical person reads about 1 year young; sensitive to creatinine (14.6 years per ln unit) | – | Already close |
| **Version 3 + Spanish recentring of c[sex]** | 0 by design | Assay alignment | Individual Spanish data with the six (or seven) markers | **Recommended path** |

- **What the recentring is.** Version 3's centring constant (`biological-age-v3.ts:335`; `MODEL-CARD.md:21`) was set on NHANES 1999–2006. A Spanish recentring sets c_es = c − mean(BA − age) on a representative Spanish adult sample, computed with the frozen model.
- **Data it needs.**
  - Albumin, ALP, hs-CRP, creatinine, urea and GGT (plus HbA1c for the second tier), measured on the same individuals.
  - Documented methods: enzymatic or corrected creatinine; albumin by BCG or BCP.
  - Echevarne alignment first (PROPOSAL condition 1).
  - About 350–410 people per sex give ±0.25 years: the SD of BA − age is 4.6 (men) and 5.0 (women) on NHANES.
  - Candidates are Di@bet.es (after re-assay), ENRICA or AEGIS, and Toledo (TSHA, 65+ only), as `DECISION.md:253` plans. Deaths are not needed for centring.
- **Expected size.** The summaries suggest c moves by +0.61 (men) and +0.26 (women) with BUN at the NHANES level, or +0.28 and −0.03 with EPIRCE BUN (`out/v3_recentring_estimate.json`). That is smaller than the ±0.7 years implied by the 6–5% spread between Spanish creatinine sources.
- **A separate product decision.** Centring on the median person would move c by about +0.4 years. Making the typical profile read its age would need about +1 year.

## 6. What EVA currently calls "average", and what should define it

**At age 45** (`out/average_definitions.md`):

| What EVA uses | Examples | Is it an average? |
|---|---|---|
| Personas (panels.json) | BUN 15 mg/dL (man) and 13 (woman); TG 140 mg/dL (man) | No; their source is undocumented. Their BUN sits at the 68th and 72nd NHANES percentiles, and only at Spanish level if EPIRCE is right |
| Seed ranges (`biomarker-ranges-en.json:2849-2857`) | BUN normal 10–25, optimal 10–18; TG optimal ≤80; hs-CRP optimal ≤0.5 | No: clinical targets |
| The model's own neutral values (deployed expected value at 45) | hs-CRP 0.62 mg/L; TG 78.7 mg/dL; creatinine 1.08 mg/dL (men) | No |
| Spanish population averages | hs-CRP 1.11 (men) / 1.59 (women) mg/L; TG 120 / 83 mg/dL; creatinine 0.94 / 0.74 mg/dL | Yes |
| Spanish sources behind today's intercepts | Bank employees; a 400-person, atherosclerosis-enriched subsample; vitamin D test requests; a TSH-truncated sample | No |

**What should define "average" for the CEO's test:**
- The target is a population average of BA − age = 0, by sex and age band.
- It should be built from population-based Spanish central values on the model's scale: ENRICA (lipids by age and sex, creatinine), SIMETAP (uric acid, HbA1c), AEGIS (hs-CRP), EPIRCE (urea).
- NHANES fills the gaps for albumin and ALP until Spanish data exist.
- For the KDM this target equals the model-scale-mean profile. For version 3 it must be computed on people, not on a profile.

## Not verified

- **Assumptions in building the profiles:**
  - Spanish levels are constant ratios along NHANES age patterns.
  - Assumed mean ages: ENRICA bands; DARIOS 51.8 (European standard population assumed); AEGIS median age used as a mean; La Rioja 50.

- **Comparability of laboratory methods** (ENRICA's Jaffé creatinine, the AEGIS "CRP" assay, EPIRCE urea) against NHANES.
- **Albumin and ALP** have no Spanish data, so the test is circular for them.
- **The KDM training sample.** The Path B script keeps ages 18 and over (`generate_path_b_full_overrides.py:59`); the rest of the cleaning is in a file on the developer's machine.

Today's deployed model does not give an average person their own age back. Version 3 nearly does.

- **Lab page today.** People with average Spanish values read older than their age at most ages. US adults read 3 to 5 years older on average.
- **The US training is not the cause.** Your test is the right one, and the US training passes it on average. With US normal values, the same US adults read within 0.6 years of their age. Three things fail: EVA's Spanish adjustment, a vitamin D unit error, and the model's straight lines across age.
- **Version 3.** A population at Spanish levels reads about half a year young or less. A single profile of typical values reads 1 to 2 years young, because version 3 gives no credit for values below its floors.
- **Creatine.** Keep creatinine as the base in both models. Start a pre-test instruction and a warning now. Neither changes a figure. Then replace today's dose formula with one flat correction taken from the trials. Bring in cystatin C later, as a calibrated option for creatine users, once Echevarne's assay and the conversion are validated.

## Does an average person get their own age back?

All figures are biological age minus age, in years, men / women. "Corrected" means rule C1, the corrected Spanish adjustment described further down.

| Who counts as average | Lab page today | Lab page corrected | Dashboard today | Dashboard corrected | Version 3 |

| EVA version 3 | Creatinine on a log scale, floors 0.8 / 0.6 mg/dL | None | `ba_v3_model.json:92-102` |

| Function Health, Ultrahuman, Thorne. NOVOS, Generation Lab, Tally | The first three do not disclose their inputs. The last three use DNA methylation | None found | Earlier review, not rechecked |

None of the models or services checked adjusts a biological age for creatine. Every blood-chemistry age keeps creatinine, except InsideTracker, which uses no kidney marker. The guidelines rely on two tools: test preparation and, where creatinine is in doubt, cystatin C.

What creatine does to EVA's figures today. The average rise in 19 trials is 0.13 mg/dL at 5 g/day, with a 95% interval of 0.07 to 0.18. The 20 g/day column uses the 0.12 mg/dL rise seen in trials of a week or less. Figures come from NHANES typical profiles at ages 30, 45 and 60.

- Doses written "5 gramos", "5 gr" or "5000 mg" get no correction. A bare "5000" gets the 0.40 mg/dL cap.
- The correction uses today's supplement list, even for labs up to 12 months old. It never touches a laboratory eGFR, which weighs 16 to 26 times as much as creatinine on the dashboard.

For B, the default should be division by 1.13. It halves the risk of over-correcting women. In men the two forms differ by less than 0.1 year.

agents.final_text:
Today's model does not give an average person their own age back. Version 3 comes much closer, but in our Spanish-level test it reads slightly young.

Three things make today's model, KDM, read wrong. EVA's Spanish adjustment pushes everyone with the standard kit older. A vitamin D unit error pushes clients with vitamin D younger. The straight lines fitted on US data miss by age, even for Americans with American values. So the US fit is part of the cause. EVA's own "typical" personas are not typical either: their urea is above the US median.

How to centre version 3 for Spain is your decision. Your target is that an average Spaniard reads their own age. EVA's recorded plan sets the level from Spanish deaths instead. The two rules can point in opposite directions.

On creatine, keep creatinine as the base in both models. Start a pre-test instruction and a warning now. The warning must quote different numbers for each figure. Then replace today's dose formula with one flat correction. Bring in cystatin C later, as a calibrated option for declared users who do not pause. We found only two precedents for basing the kidney part of an age on cystatin C: one published UK Biobank panel and one consumer service.

Today's model will stay for about a year, and a physician may refuse to sign any change to it. I recommend withholding the lab-page figure until version 3, because it has the largest errors. Keep the dashboard figure as a labelled estimate.

| Question | Answer | Key figures: biological age minus real age, years, men / women |
|---|---|---|
| Does an average Spaniard read their own age on the lab page today? | No | US people moved to Spanish average levels, urea at the US level: +1.86 / +1.43 overall, up to +4.97 / +4.35 at ages 20 to 29. If Spanish urea is 29% higher, as one study says: +9.42 / +6.71 |

Review of 6c3d251..54ead22. I found five confirmed problems: one medium, four low. Three are in production behaviour, one is in production behaviour but can only happen after a database read fails, and one is a test that checks less than it claims. The repository is unmodified. `tsc` is clean and the full suite passes (895 tests). The reproductions are in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-eva-health/4e1a7523-c199-547a-904f-d87e53286958/scratchpad/review4/`. Run them from that folder with `npx vitest run --config vitest.config.mts <file>`.

## Findings

**1. The dashboard's rolling average checks creatinine at the wrong point** — `src/lib/biomarkers/rolling-average-ba.ts:313-328` (check at `biological-age-kdm.ts:777`). Severity: medium.
- **What goes wrong:** the 0.2–15 mg/dL check sits inside `applyLifestyleAdjustments`. Processing and version 3 run it on each lab's measured value. The dashboard reaches it only after each lab has been divided by its creatine divisor and the labs averaged. So a bad measured value can reach the main figure users see, and a valid one can block it.
- **Scenarios** (fake database, Base Panel of the typical man of 45):
  - Two ready labs with creatinine 1.0 and 0.09 (a unit or decimal error). The 0.09 lab gets no figure on the lab page, but the dashboard shows **45.35**. That is computed from an average creatinine of 0.545; the good lab alone gives 47.20.
  - One lab measured at 16 mg/dL, creatine 5 g/day. No figure on the lab page; the dashboard shows **100.7** (16 / 1.13 = 14.2, which passes).
  - One lab measured at 0.2 mg/dL, creatine 5 g/day. The lab page has a figure (the commit's own test says 0.2 is plausible), but the dashboard is null (0.2 / 1.13 = 0.177).
- **Reproduction:** `rolling/plausibility.test.ts` (3 failing tests).
- **Fix:** in `computeRollingAverageBA`, drop creatinine rows whose measured value fails `isPlausibleCreatinineMgDl` before `adjustCreatinineByLab` and averaging. Do not re-check the adjusted average.

**2. The creatine dose reader silently misreads realistic inputs** — `src/lib/biomarkers/supplements.ts:262-307`. Severity: low.
- **What goes wrong:** a number is returned in every case below, so the context form shows no "cannot read" message.
  - A weekly count it cannot parse is read as a weekly total. "5 g tres días a la semana", "5 g, 3 por semana", "5 g three times a week" and "5 g 3x/week" all give **0.71** instead of 2.14 g/day (divisor 1.031 instead of 1.093). The weekly-total rule (`WEEKLY_TOTAL`, :307) fires because the days-per-week rule needs a digit followed by días/veces.
  - "4 cápsulas x 750 mg" gives **0.75** instead of 3. The capsule pattern accepts only "de/of" (:274).
  - A training note is read as the dosing frequency: "5 g al día (entreno 3 días a la semana)" gives 2.14 instead of 5.
  - "x N" is multiplied in even when N is days or a duration (:268). "5 g x 3 días a la semana" gives 6.43 (the 3 counts twice); "2,5 g x 30 días" gives 75.
  - Frequency words are ignored. "2,5 g dos veces al día" and "2.5 g twice a day" give 2.5 instead of 5.
  - Ranges can read the upper end: "2-3 cápsulas de 750 mg" gives 2.25.
- **Impact:** for the man of 45 at creatinine 1.13, the stored biological age (the lab-page figure) is 52.23 instead of 51.62 for "tres días", and 52.21 instead of 51.29 for "4 cápsulas x 750 mg".
- **Reproduction:** `dose/dose.test.ts` (8 failing tests).
- **Fix:** when a frequency phrase is present but its count cannot be read, return null. Accept "N cápsulas x M unit". Do not multiply "x N" when N is followed by días/semanas/meses/veces. Read the number words uno–siete, one–seven and twice.

**3. A failed recompute leaves a ready lab out of the dashboard** — `src/app/api/lab-results/[id]/context/route.ts:179` and `src/lib/lab-results/auto-resolve.ts:125`. Severity: low.
- **What goes wrong:** in both flows the dashboard refresh happens only as the last step of `recomputeLabMetrics` (`process-results.ts:758`). If an earlier step throws, the lab is ready but `profiles.current_ba` is never refreshed. That is now likelier, because `loadLabSupplements` (:719) throws on a read error, and the lab update can also throw (:745). The cached figure was computed on arrival, while the lab was still `pending_context`, so it excludes the lab until another lab or edit. The route comment "a failure keeps the figures from arrival" is not true for the dashboard.
- **Reproduction:** `context/skip-refresh.test.ts`, a copy of the commit's context-route test with a transient error on the lab read. The route returns 200 and the lab is ready, but there are 0 updates to `profiles`.
- **Fix:** call `recomputeAndCacheUserBA` when the recompute fails, or wrap steps 4–5 of `recomputeLabMetrics` in try/finally so the refresh always runs.

**4. The auto-resolve test does not check what it claims** — `src/lib/lab-results/auto-resolve.test.ts:44-50`. Severity: low.
- **What goes wrong:** the test says the recompute happens "once it is ready". It computes `readyAt` but never compares it with the recompute; it only checks the recompute ran after `generateSummary`.
- **Reproduction:** `autoresolve/auto-resolve.ts` is a copy with the recompute moved above the ready update. The copied test file still passes all 6 tests against it.
- **Fix:** record `calls.length` inside the `recomputeLabMetrics` mock and assert it is greater than `readyAt`.

**5. Auto-resolve now recomputes under an empty context after a read error** — `src/lib/lab-results/auto-resolve.ts:59-65` and `:125`. Severity: low.
- **What goes wrong:** `getCurrentVersion(...).catch(() => null)` turns a read error into "no context". The cron then creates an empty version and stamps it on the lab; this part existed before. New in this range, the stored KDM and version 3 figures are then recomputed under that empty context. A client declaring 5 g/day loses the adjustment on that lab, and the empty version becomes their current context. This goes against the commits' rule that reads throw instead of falling back.
- **Reproduction:** `autoresolve/fallback.test.ts`. It passes, showing the lab stamped with `v-empty` and `recomputeLabMetrics` called.
- **Fix:** let the error propagate. The cron already leaves the lab pending and retries it.

## Checked and found correct

## Review of 6c3d251..54ead22 against the review findings

Two notes on scope. The results file holds **28** confirmed findings, not 27: 7 code, 13 clinical and 8 dataflow. All 28 are covered below. At HEAD (54ead22), vitest passes 895/895 and `tsc --noEmit` is clean. My scripts and outputs are in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-eva-health/4e1a7523-c199-547a-904f-d87e53286958/scratchpad/review4b/` (numbers.ts, dash.ts, count.ts, parser.ts, rolling_plaus.ts, mutate.mjs with mutations.json, NUMBERS.head.md, KDM-EXPLAIN.head.md, abstracts/).

### The 28 findings

|---|---|---|
| code-1 | Resolved | `[id]/context/route.ts:173-181` and `auto-resolve.ts:125` call recomputeLabMetrics after the lab is set to ready. `context-route.test.ts:118` checks the 5 g figures, v3 `creatine_g_per_day` 5 and the dashboard cache. Removing either call fails a test (mutations C1, C2). |

### The two deliberate differences

**KDM-EXPLAIN-PANELS.md as a historical snapshot: acceptable.** The file is internal and no page cites it. It was already stale after the 25 September fixes (`BA-INPUT-FIXES.md:332`). Regenerating it would remove the "before" figures that `ba_input_fixes_report.ts` checks against. The note's numbers hold: `scripts/kdm_explain_panels.ts` run to a scratch file gives the athlete's Comprehensive figure as 36.2, and the file shows 44.6 with eGFR +9.5. One wrinkle: line 11 still says "The deployed KDM biological age, unchanged".

**The undated "…hasta que se recalculan" sentence: true, and better than guessing a date, but not actionable.**
- It is the right call while the deploy date is unknown.
- A reader still cannot tell which figure is old, because the dashboard cache has no tag.
- "Until recalculated" suggests every figure will be recalculated. Lab pages are only recalculated on a value edit or an admin recalc.
- It sits only in the kidney paragraph, not next to the creatine-formula change.

Suggested fix: run `scripts/backfill_rolling_average_ba.ts` at deploy (it writes only `profiles.current_ba*`) and add the date once known. Optionally, label lab-page figures tagged `KDM_REFERENCE_BA_METHOD_BEFORE_R2`; the constant exists but is unused.

### Numbers checked

Everything below reproduces unless listed under new problems.
- **Base Panel, Reference version, undeclared creatine:** +1.23 to +1.65 at a 13% rise, and +1.27 to +2.01 at +0.13 mg/dL, so "entre 1 y 2" holds. The counsel note's range "1.23 to 2.01" takes its ends from the two different assumptions. With a full panel the range is +0.83 to +1.26, so "algo menos" holds.
- **Typical man and woman of 45:** 1.27/1.23 on the lab page, 0.53/0.63 on the dashboard, 1.78 in v3.
- **Woman at +0.13 mg/dL:** 1.64 undeclared, 0.36 after declaring, and 2.33/0.55 in v3.
- **Loaded client on 2 g:** 0.39 on the lab page, 0.57 in v3.
- **5 g declared with no rise yet:** −1.12 on the lab page, −1.78 in v3.
- **Marker count:** the Base Panel's Comprehensive figure uses 12 of its 13 tests.
- **CYSTATIN header:** the −7.2 to +0.7 range holds, and the reader handles "5 gramos", "5 gr" and "5000 mg".
- **Sources:** Tsiaras (0.13 mg/dL, 95% CI 0.07–0.18, n = 19), Hultman and Vilar Neto were checked against their Europe PMC abstracts.
- **Not re-run:** the 1.65 and 0.775 evaluation figures predate the change and need data I did not have.

### New problems

**N1 (low–medium).** `rolling-average-ba.ts:239-254, :314`, together with `biological-age-kdm.ts:777`.
- **What is wrong:** the plausibility check runs on the creatinine averaged across labs, not on each lab.
- **Reproduced (rolling_plaus.ts):**
  - Labs with creatinine 1.0 and 88.4 average 44.70, so both Comprehensive and Reference return null.
  - `recomputeAndCacheUserBA` then caches null (`:373`), and the dashboard falls back to the latest lab's stored figure, or shows nothing (`dashboard-client.tsx:310`).
  - With seven labs the average is 13.49, which passes the check and caches 97.97 for a man of 45.
- **Fix:** in `adjustCreatinineByLab`, set out-of-range creatinine rows to NaN, which `averageBiomarkers` skips, and add a test.

**N2 (low).** `completa/page.tsx:172, :288` cite Kreider 2017 for "la creatina eleva la creatinina… sin cambiar el filtrado renal medido".
- **What is wrong:** Kreider's renal section (full text PMC5469049) reports GFR unchanged in Poortmans' studies. For its own trial it reports "no significant effects on creatinine", which contradicts the rise.
- **Fix:** cite Tsiaras (reference 9) for the rise.

**N3 (low).** `completa:172, :288`: "3 a 5 g al día sin carga, porque el músculo tarda unas cuatro semanas (Hultman 1996)".
- **What is wrong:** Hultman's abstract gives 28 days for 3 g/day only; 5 g/day was not studied.
- **Fix:** "con 3 g al día, unas cuatro semanas".

**N4 (nit).** `CALIBRATION-AND-CREATINE.md:11` says the woman's dashboard figure rises 0.62. It reproduces as 0.6275 (46.286 → 46.914, dash.ts), so it should read 0.63.

**N5 (low).** Three route changes have no test. Each of these mutations leaves 895/895 green:
- removing the context stamp in enter-results (`route.ts:54`);
- removing the cache refresh in confirm (`confirm/route.ts:232`);
- removing the cache refresh in reprocess (`reprocess/route.ts:254`).

**Fix:** add route tests like `context-route.test.ts`.

**N6 (nit).** `labs-client.tsx:361/372`: "Esta cifra usa el contexto registrado con esta analítica".
- **What is wrong:** the note also shows under new-rule figures of labs with no recorded context. Those read the version in force when the lab was entered, or none (`lab-context.ts:7-8`). Examples: a legacy lab recomputed after a value edit, or an upload confirmed without a context id.
- **Fix:** "el contexto vigente cuando se registró esta analítica".

**N7 (nit).** Two dose forms are misread silently, with no form message:
- "5 g los días de entreno (3 por semana)" reads as 0.71 g/day, because `WEEKLY_TOTAL` (`supplements.ts:248`) wins over the days-per-week rule.
- "1 g mañana y 1 g noche" reads as 1 g.

No tracked file changed (`git status` is clean). `tsc --noEmit` refreshed the git-ignored `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo`. A `__pycache__` created by `py_compile` was removed.

That breaks the contract this range wrote into its own docstring, and the range applied the throw-on-error rule to every comparable read except this one. The suggested fix is right in substance; I'd use `.maybeSingle()` rather than exempting PGRST116 by hand.

**Why it's a defect and not a design choice**
- **Old read, new contract:** the read at `process-results.ts:675-679` predates the range (it's the same at 82fd5cc). But this range changed the docstring (:640-647) from "Throws only if the lab_results UPDATE fails" to "Throws if a read the figures need ... fails; the stored figures are then left as they were".
- **The sibling read was fixed:** this range changed the identical profile read in `rolling-average-ba.ts:274-279` to throw on error. The range also made `loadLabSupplements`/`loadLabContext` throw, and v3 stores `{reason:"error"}` when it fails. This read is the gap left by the earlier "read errors" fix.
- **New callers rely on the throw:** the context route (:180), the cron's opsAlert (`auto-resolve.ts:127`) and the per-lab repair (`recalc-metrics/route.ts:56`).
- **The deliberate path is untouched:** "no usable profile → zone counts only, v3 `sex_unknown`" is tested and intended for incomplete profiles. The fix keeps it.
- **The failure is realistic:** postgrest-js 2.101.1 returns a network failure as `{data:null, error}` rather than throwing, so a dropped connection silently becomes "no profile".

**What the client and the docs see**
- After the failed recompute, the lab's figure still carries the `KDM_v2.2_ReferenceBA_r2` tag, so `labs-client.tsx:423` shows the creatine note: "Esta cifra usa el contexto guardado con esta analítica". The saved context is V2 (5 g creatine), but the figure was computed under V1, so it reads 1.27 years older and nothing repairs it.
- `APPLIED.md` promises the lab is recomputed, v3 record included, once its context is confirmed. Instead the v3 record gets a false `sex_unknown` reason.
- The repair and backfill route reports the lab as `ok`.
- One nuance: the dashboard and the lab page use different models, so their numbers always differ. The real mismatch is that they were computed under different contexts (V2 vs V1).

# EVA Health: CMO reassessment and next steps

Date: 3 November 2026
For: the CEO
Prepared by: the orchestrator, an AI acting as CMO; a licensed physician must review and countersign the clinical decisions in it.

This memo draws on six AI reviews, an AI fact-check and an AI critique, checked against the repo, the live site and cited sources on 3 November; no clinician has checked it. Efforts and dates are planning estimates. Tags such as E4 point to section 7.

## 1. Bottom line

This week, keep both databases paused, switch off the scheduled jobs and remove every public claim EVA cannot support. No client can see a result today, so the live exposure is the website and any result sent before the pause. The website calls the biological age a validated mortality prediction, promises critical-result alerts that nothing delivers, and lists seven markers EVA does not order. If the app came back on today's code, a Base Panel client could be shown a biological age 13 to 36 years too old, and the AI prompt on record asks for named prescription drugs and doses. Before anyone logs in again, ship a safe mode: measured values and the laboratory's signed report, with no biological age, no score and no AI advice. Contract a licensed physician with a veto and health-regulatory counsel now, because no human is clinically accountable for anything EVA shows. Version 3 is the right model, but its first venous result is about April 2027 at the earliest, so for now only send Echevarne the method questions and commission an independent human replication.

- Fact 4 was not re-checked. Paid Supabase projects cannot be paused, so production has no point-in-time recovery.
- Fact 7: about 0.4 of the 0.9 and 0.8 years is US population weighting. The Spanish part uses no Spanish albumin or ALP data, and its scripts are not in the repo.
